who_can_apply: Sophomores (80 to 90 credits) and juniors (140 to 150 credits by January) with a 2.0 GPA or higher, good attendance, Algebra I or Integrated Math I done, and currently in Geometry or higher.
how_to_apply: Register for the Evergreen Valley College placement test at (408) 274-7900 x6636, attend a recruitment and info meeting to get the application, then mail it or hand-deliver it to the Roble Building mailroom at Evergreen Valley College.
notes: Page lists no age rule and no 2026-27 meeting dates; call the coordinator (Kathleen Leal, (408) 274-7900 x6881) for the schedule. Must also be taking biology, chemistry and physics and English 2 (sophomores) or English 3 (juniors).
duration: 2 years
pay_detail: No cost listed on the page (public school program)

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21, currently in high school or college. Alameda County program. No income or residency rule is listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Call the Alameda County Workforce Development Board main line at (510) 259-3842. You can also use the Contact Us link on the youth page.
notes: Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 use the Future Force program instead. The youth page says to find a local Future Force provider through its Future Force page. The youth page lists no individual provider phone numbers.
pay_detail: Not stated. The youth page mentions paid and unpaid work experience but gives no wage.

who_can_apply: Girls in 11th grade who are selected and sponsored by a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit. Each high school may have only one delegate. If a school has no sponsoring Unit, a student can apply as a Department (statewide) alternate applicant. Age rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor or contact a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit (the site has a spreadsheet to find one). Each Unit picks a delegate and two alternates. Students at schools with no sponsoring Unit can use the START HERE online application as Department alternate applicants.
notes: Separate from the coed American Legion California Boys State (Boys & Girls State) program, which has its own card on this site. The FAQ says a student may apply to either American Legion CA Boys State or American Legion Auxiliary CA Girls State, but not both. Selection criteria, grade-school rules beyond the 11th grade note, and cost are not stated on the pages.
duration: One week. The 2026 session (83rd) ran June 22-27, 2026.
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program pages. The site says there are opportunities for scholarship consideration, including the Samsung American Legion Scholarship.

who_can_apply: Ages 10 and up. Teens 15 to 17 may volunteer on their own. Under 15 needs an adult (1 adult for every 5 youth).
how_to_apply: Book shifts on the volunteer calendar or email volunteer@accfb.org, phone 510-635-3663 ext. 308.
notes: 7900 Edgewater Dr, Oakland. Wear closed-toe shoes that cover your whole foot. BART to Coliseum, then AC Transit 98.
duration: Shifts

who_can_apply: Not stated on the page. Ages and requirements vary by role and are shown on the portal.
how_to_apply: Browse and apply on the library's Better Impact volunteer portal. The link is on the page. The library phone is 510-745-1500.
notes: The teen page is thin and does not name a teen role or branch. Ask the Fremont Main Library which roles take teens.

who_can_apply: Teens. The TAG page does not state an age or grade. Other teen volunteer roles on the same page use grades 7 to 12 or ages 12 to 17.
how_to_apply: Complete the online TAG registration form on the library page. Questions: refdesk@alamedaca.gov or (510) 747-7777.
notes: Meets at the Main Library in the Stafford Room. The page states no age rule, so ask the library if you are younger than 12 or older than 17. See also Alameda Free Library Teen Volunteers (Book Reviewers and Coding with LEGO) for volunteer roles such as book reviews and LEGO coding.
duration: 1st Tuesday of the month, 4:30 to 5:30 pm
pay_detail: Community service hours only

who_can_apply: Teen Book Reviewers: grades 7 to 12. Coding with LEGO: ages 12 to 17.
how_to_apply: LEGO program: email Fernanda Nunez at fnunez@alamedaca.gov. Book reviews: use the 'How to become a Book Reviewer' page linked from the teen page. Questions: refdesk@alamedaca.gov or 510-747-7777.
notes: Book reviews are limited to one a month. No coding experience needed for LEGO. See also Alameda Free Library Teen Advisory Group (TAG) for the advisory role, where teens suggest ideas for library events and projects.
pay_detail: Community service hours only

who_can_apply: Local youth, especially students in Alameda Unified School District career technical education programs.
how_to_apply: No sign-up is listed; admission is free. Contacts: Jennifer Padilla (City) 510-747-6852; Amanda Vigil (AUSD) 510-337-7091.
notes: Held at Encinal Jr/Sr High, 210 Central Ave, Alameda. It is an annual fair, but the 2027 date has not been posted.
duration: One afternoon
pay_detail: Free to attend. The fair covers part-time jobs and internships, but the page does not say if they are paid.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 16. Applicants complete an online application and an on-site interview, then required trainings. Both a parent and the teen sign liability forms.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application during an open window, attend an interview, then the online and on-site training days.
notes: Spring and Fall sessions are weekends only; Summer shifts run seven days a week. The Aquarium also lists other youth roles for ages 11 to 18 (Ocean Neighbors, Teen Science Cafe Volunteer, Student Eco-Ambassadors). The Education Volunteer role is for ages 16 and up with at least 100 hours in six months.
duration: 60 hours over a 10-week session (Spring, Summer or Fall), one shift a day each week, 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program (60 service hours).

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 at Center, Del Campo, El Camino Fundamental or Inderkum High School who meet federal rules for financial need and/or being first in the family to go to college, and want to go beyond high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Upward Bound application, then staff review eligibility and interview the student and family if eligible. Contact arctrioub@arc.losrios.edu or (916) 484-8033 (Mon to Fri, 9 am to 6 pm).
notes: Only for students at the four listed partner schools. Summer participation is required. The dedicated application page did not show details when read. Ask staff for current dates.
duration: Year-round, including a required summer component
pay_detail: Free program. No stipend mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 14 and a half years old. The page lists this rule for all volunteers and links a separate Teen Volunteer Application.
how_to_apply: Complete the Teen Volunteer Application (Google form on the page). Questions: armc-volunteers@armc.sbcounty.gov or Volunteer Management, 400 N. Pepper Avenue, Colton, CA 92324.
notes: Minimum age is 14 and a half. The page lists no application deadline or start dates.
duration: At least 100 hours; one 2-hour shift a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18 who start tasks on their own. You like the arts and feel at ease with kids.
how_to_apply: Use the Learn More and Sign Up link on the volunteer page, which opens a Google Form. You can also call the Armory at (626) 792-5101.
notes: Hours and session dates are not on the page. The Armory's Fall Studio 2026 classes are on a separate page.
duration: Each Studio session (hours not listed)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: At least 16 years old, and enrolled in high school or college (or enrolled within the past 12 months). A community group must sponsor your placement.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply to BART directly. Ask a community organization or your school to sponsor you and have them email workforcedevelopment@bart.gov.
notes: Sponsor organizations fund the placements. Build a relationship with a community group and ask them to contact workforcedevelopment@bart.gov.
duration: June 22 to July 31, 2026, 10 to 20 hours a week
pay_detail: $20 per hour (high school, 2026)

who_can_apply: Berkeley High students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe enrollment. Contact CTE Manager Wyn Skeels, WynSkeels@berkeley.net, (510) 644-8727, or your counselor.
notes: Pathway classes meet the a-g rules for getting into college. Middle schoolers get a STEM exploration track.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Age 12 or older. Ages 12 to 15 must have a parent or guardian with them 1 to 1. Age 16 and up can volunteer alone with a release form.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a General Volunteer Orientation online, read the manual, attend orientation. Contact volunteer@berkeleyhumane.org, (510) 845-7735.
notes: Internships need 18 or older (10 to 20 plus hours a week for 3 months or more).

who_can_apply: Finished 10th or 11th grade, 3.0 GPA, 16 by June 21 (2026 rule).
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Pre-College Scholars site. The 2026 window opened Feb 2, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
notes: Very expensive. Aid is limited. Also needs a 3.0 GPA and good standing at your school.
duration: 6 or 8 weeks
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $15,987 (8 weeks, June 22 to Aug 14) or $14,687 (6 weeks, July 6 to Aug 14). There is also an application fee. One media scholarship was offered in 2026.

who_can_apply: Teen volunteer: fill out the application. No age is stated. Youth Worker: ages 14 to 25. No experience is needed. A work permit is required if under 18.
how_to_apply: Volunteers: complete the Teen Volunteer Application form. Paid work: go through Berkeley YouthWorks (2180 Milvia St, 510-981-4970); see the YouthWorks page for the current interest form.
notes: The library page also lists other groups that take teen volunteers. Berkeley YouthWorks serves Berkeley residents. You must show proof that you live there. The library page says YouthWorks takes applications in March and October.
duration: Youth Worker up to 15 hours a week
pay_detail: Volunteering is unpaid. Youth Worker jobs are paid (rate not posted; no benefits).

who_can_apply: Bay Area high school students. A new group starts at the beginning of each school year.
how_to_apply: Join the Teen Council mailing list on the Teen Council page, or email teencouncil@berkeleyrep.org.
notes: No grade or age rule is listed beyond high school. Competitive: only 10 to 15 spots.
pay_detail: Transportation stipend. Free admission to teen programs and shows, and free food at events.

who_can_apply: Berkeley residents (proof of residency at onboarding). Priority for youth facing barriers, such as foster care or legal system involvement, English learners, young parents, and students with IEPs or 504 plans. The page states no age rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online YouthWorks interest form. Chosen candidates get an email for a 15 to 20 minute interview. Contact: youthworks@berkeleyca.gov, (510) 981-4970.
notes: An interest form does not guarantee a placement. Berkeley Public Library lists the Youth Worker age as 14 to 25. Berkeley residents only.
duration: Winter 2027 placements run January to March 2027
pay_detail: Wage not posted. Ready to Work workshop stipend if you attend at least 7 of 8 sessions.

who_can_apply: Current and former foster youth in Alameda County, per the homepage (it says it serves over 500 each year). The age range and intake steps are not stated on the pages.
how_to_apply: Call 510.980.9010 or email info@beyondemancipation.org (both from the site footer). Staff connect youth to coaching, training and job resources.
notes: Corrected on 2026-10-07. The site loaded this time (the earlier certificate error is gone). The homepage and employment page say who is served and what coaching covers, but do not state an age range, costs or an intake process, so those are left blank or not stated. This is a coaching service rather than a paid job, so the type is the closest available. The employment page lists outside job boards and training partners (Civicorps, Oakland Private Industry Council, EASTBAY Works), which are separate organizations. The jobs page is for B:E staff openings, not youth jobs. Call before relying on it.
pay_detail: No pay to the youth is stated. The cost of services to the youth is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who have been Club members for 2 or more years and meet academic requirements. The page does not list the academic requirements.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Ask staff at your Clubhouse. The site lists a 3300 High Street address.
notes: The same Teens page lists Keystone Clubs (ages 14 to 18) and Youth of the Year (ages 16 to 18, a $20,000 scholarship opportunity, not a job). They are not separate cards because the page gives no joining steps. Staff openings are posted on LinkedIn (the careers page does not list them). Season, pay rate, hours and deadlines are not stated, so confirm with the Club before a teen applies. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
pay_detail: The page says 'Paid positions and income.' The pay rate and hours are not stated.

who_can_apply: The page says Breakthrough uses college and high school students as teachers and tutors. No age or grade rule for teachers is posted. Students attend the summer program before 7th, 8th or 9th grade.
how_to_apply: Use the Teaching Intern application link on breakthroughsac.org (online account login). Questions: BSAC@BreakthroughSac.org or 916-234-3905.
notes: Age minimum, pay and dates are not posted on the site, so call or email before applying. Training is two weeks (80 hours) on site.
duration: 6-week summer program
pay_detail: Pay not stated. Ask the program.

who_can_apply: High school students who completed junior year and have a semester left. There is no application. Your school recommends you. A local American Legion Post interviews and sponsors you. Girls State (below) is a separate program.
how_to_apply: Tell your counselor in junior year you are interested, or contact a local American Legion Post (use Find-A-Post on calegion.org). The Post chooses delegates; the delegate then registers online.
notes: Two separate programs. This one has been coed since 2023. California Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary, cagirlsstate.org) is its own program. It ran June 22 to 27, 2026 for 11th graders sponsored by a local Auxiliary Unit, one delegate per school. You can apply to only one. An old note about a 2020 article and a Sanger phone was out of date.
duration: One week in June at Sacramento State. The site counts down to June 19, 2027.
pay_detail: Registration fee listed as $550 per delegate on the Key Dates page (the page does not label the year). Ask your sponsoring Post who pays.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 21, per the 2026 Explorer competition packet. This is the competition age rule. Post membership rules such as GPA or background checks are not stated on the pages.
how_to_apply: Email CHPExplorers@chp.ca.gov or call (916) 843-3210 (both listed in the 2026 packet) to ask how to join a post near you.
notes: Both official pages were read on 2026-10-07. The page covers the statewide competition and does not say how to join a post. The 2026 packet is the source for the 15 to 21 age rule, which it states for the competition. Whether a post near you has room, and any background check or GPA rule, must be asked of CHP. The CHP East Sacramento post page returns 403 to automated reads, so use the email or phone above. See also CHP Explorer Post (East Sacramento) for a local post. Ages differ by source: the 2026 competition packet says 15 to 21, while the CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers.
duration: Not stated for post membership. The 2026 competition ran April 25 to 26, 2026.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cost to you: 2026 competition fees were $150 per explorer, $125 per advisor and $75 per spectator.

who_can_apply: California law says an apprentice must be at least 16 (Labor Code 3077, in the state child labor guide). Each registered program sets its own minimum age, education and tests, shown in the DAS search, and may set a higher age.
how_to_apply: Use the Apprenticeship Search on the DAS site, check each program's minimum age and requirements, and apply the way the listing says.
notes: The DAS homepage states no age rule. The 16 minimum comes from the 2013 DLSE child labor guide, which also says apprentices need a school-issued work permit. DAS's How to Become an Apprentice page says search results list each program's minimum age. DAS runs a youth apprenticeship grant and reports 5,776 registered pre-apprentices on its homepage.
pay_detail: DAS describes apprenticeship as earn-and-learn. Wages depend on the program; DAS has a tool to look up apprenticeship wages.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 15 to 25 who need extra help to finish school or find work. Examples listed are offense history as a minor and teen parent. Others are foster care or no stable housing, and gang involvement or risk. Minority group, low income, and disability or reading difficulty are also listed. You may still qualify if you do not match these.
how_to_apply: The page has no separate enrollment steps. Use the YEOP Contact Information page. It helps you reach a YEOP specialist in your area. Or contact your local America's Job Center of California.
notes: The page says clearly: this is not a job placement program. It is help and coaching toward school and work.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: No pay. The page does not say whether services cost anything.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 24 who meet certain requirements. The EDD page does not list the requirements. It points to the Youth Employment Opportunity Program page and fact sheet for criteria.
how_to_apply: Find your local America's Job Center of California with the EDD Office Locator (edd.ca.gov/en/Office_Locator/). The page also suggests building a resume in CalJOBS and visiting the center to ask about internships, apprenticeships and training.
notes: The EDD page does not say the youth services are free. It says Job Centers connect employers with job seekers at no cost. Eligibility criteria are not on the EDD page; it links to the YEOP services and eligibility criteria. Teens under 18 who take a paid job in California need a work permit from their school (CDE page).
duration: Ongoing, set by each local center
pay_detail: The services are free (the page says Job Centers connect employers with job seekers at no cost). Work experience can be paid or unpaid; no pay rate is given.

who_can_apply: Under 18 needs written parent or guardian permission. Specific age minimums vary by park.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the State Parks volunteer portal or print a paper application and mail it to the park you want. Questions: Volunteer.inparksprogram@parks.ca.gov or (916) 653-9069. The application link is on the official page.
notes: A criminal background check may be required. Park-level age minimums were not on the page, so ask the park. Student volunteer or intern roles are mentioned only as a general possibility at local parks. No Junior Ranger details were on this page.
duration: Varies by park
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 30 on the first day of service. You must meet at least one of: foster care, justice involved, mental health or substance abuse system, low income, hard time finding work, or unemployed and/or out of school.
how_to_apply: Pick your local program from the partner list on the state page and apply through its link. Or use the state interest form. State office: info@californiavolunteers.ca.gov (say Youth Service Corps) or (916) 323-7646.
notes: Partner list on the page: Anaheim, Antioch, Bakersfield, Chula Vista, Fresno, Irvine, La Puente, Long Beach, Los Angeles, Oakland, Rancho Cucamonga, Riverside, Sacramento, San Francisco, San Diego, San Jose, Santa Cruz, South Gate, Stockton, Marin County, Monterey County, Mechoopda Band of Chico Rancheria and Ramona Band of Cahuilla. California requires a work permit for minors in paid jobs (CDE page), so under 18 you will need one. The state page does not say whether each city requires you to live there, so check the local program.
duration: Not stated on the state page; set by each local program
pay_detail: At least minimum wage; the rate varies by location (page wording).

who_can_apply: Your school district must run an approved WEE program. Exploratory WEE students can be as young as 12 and do not need a work permit. General WEE usually needs a work permit. Career Technical WEE needs a job related to a career technical class you take.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor or CTE/work experience coordinator whether your district has a WEE program and what class goes with it.
notes: The 2013 state child labor guide says students must be 16 to enroll in WEE, with exceptions in the Education Code (14 and 15 year olds can get permits in some cases). The CDE page says Exploratory can start at 12. Programs exist only where the district chose to run one. Use the three current names above.
pay_detail: Exploratory is unpaid. General and Career Technical WEE combine paid work with a class.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors interested in engineering, robotics or AI. Bonita Unified School District students get priority.
how_to_apply: Email the RASIM Center at rasim@cpp.edu to sign up during the January to April window.
notes: The page's sample schedule is labeled Summer 2027 but gives no exact dates. Confirm by email.
duration: Held each July, daily 9:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., at Cal Poly Pomona Building 17
pay_detail: $25 per person. Parking permit and daily lunch included.

who_can_apply: Kids and teens join through a county 4-H program. Check your county page for age rules and fees.
how_to_apply: Find your county 4-H office from ucanr.edu/sites/ca4H.
notes: The 4-H site blocked automated access on 2026-10-07 (403 and a bot check), so age rules and fees could not be read. Ages, fees and teen roles must be confirmed with your county 4-H office. Re-checked on 2026-10-09: the 4-H page returned HTTP 403 again, so it could not be read and the card stays snippet-only.
duration: Club year
pay_detail: Not confirmed. Fees depend on the county program.

who_can_apply: Students at a school that runs a California Cadet Corps unit. Participation is voluntary. The pages do not say how a student enrolls beyond being at a host school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school whether it has a Cadet Corps unit. The program site says schools that want to start one should email Recruiting@cacadets.org. The site's Contact Us page is cacadets.org/about/contact.
notes: Program pages did not include a school finder, so the best first step is to ask your school office or email the program. The program site says more than 7,000 students are in over 100 schools.
duration: Ongoing school year program
pay_detail: Free. The program site says it is fully funded by the state with no cost to families or host schools. Cadets earn up to ten elective credits per year.

who_can_apply: Students at a California school with an FBLA chapter. The FAQ says FBLA is open to students enrolled in a Career and Technical Education (CTE) business program.
how_to_apply: Ask whether your school has a chapter: email hello@cafbla.org or call (714) 824-4489. If not, fill out the FBLA Interest Form so staff can help your school affiliate; that needs your school administration.
notes: You join through a school chapter, so you need a business pathway or class at your school. If your school has no business program, the FAQ says starting one has to be started with school administration.
duration: Ongoing through the school year
pay_detail: Not a job. The join page lists no dues amounts.

who_can_apply: Join through a school that has an agricultural education program; chapters are chartered in schools with ag classes. California reports over 103,000 members. The pages do not state age or grade rules.
how_to_apply: Take an agriculture class at a school with an FFA chapter.
notes: Not every school has an FFA chapter. Ask your counselor or ag teacher. Age and grade limits and dues were not on the California or National FFA pages checked.
duration: School year; SAE can be year-round
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the program pages. Ask your ag teacher what your chapter charges.

who_can_apply: Students at schools that host an academy. Each academy has its own way to apply. Look on the school's website for 'Partnership Academy'.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor if your school has an academy. The CDE page links a directory of academies (a spreadsheet updated September 2026). The page does not say how students apply.
notes: Read the CDE page on 2026-10-09. It confirms a three-year program for grades 10 to 12, structured as a school-within-a-school, with academics plus career technical education, business partnerships, mentoring and internships. It posts only school and district grant dates, not student application dates, and does not say whether students from other districts may transfer in. Academies are run by individual schools, so ask your counselor. Fremont Unified says some CTE courses sit inside Partnership Academies.
duration: 3 years
pay_detail: The CDE page does not say whether internships pay or give school credit. Ask the school.

who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled in a Pasadena Unified School District (PUSD) high school. Grade and age rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: The page has no form. Use the email link for the program contact (Mitch Aiken) on the Summer Research Connection page.
notes: Only for PUSD students. Contact early in the school year because spots fill by early spring.
duration: 6 weeks
pay_detail: The page does not say whether interns are paid or what it costs. Ask the program contact.

who_can_apply: High school students who meet at least one criterion, such as low income, foster youth, system-involved, homeless, pregnant or parenting, English learner, below grade level in math or reading, or an IEP.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Referral Form (online form linked on the CCCOE page) or call: West County (925) 296-1507 or 296-1504; East County (925) 296-1505 or 296-1506.
notes: The out-of-school program is for ages 18 to 24, so only the in-school program fits most teens. Help can include transportation, interview clothes and school supplies.
pay_detail: Paid workforce prep and work experience (rate not posted)

who_can_apply: Students 14 to 18 enrolled in high school with a transcript showing at least a 3.2 GPA. New volunteers and one parent or guardian must attend a mandatory in-person Teen Information Session.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with your transcript, finish the online volunteer orientation, complete health screening and flu vaccine (flu season Nov 1 to Apr 30), and attend the Teen Information Session (Monday, Jan 11, 2027, 5:30 to 7:00 p.m.).
notes: Spots are limited and fill fast, so apply the day the window opens. Shifts run Monday to Sunday. Teens who want research should look at Cedars-Sinai's separate INSPIRE Internship Program (not checked here). Questions: TeenVolunteerProgram@cshs.org or 310-423-8044.
duration: Winter/Spring and Fall: one 2-hour shift a week for 10 weeks (20 hours). Summer: two 4-hour shifts a week for 5 weeks (40 hours).
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers buy the required volunteer jacket for $30 (cash) and wear black or white scrubs.

who_can_apply: Current high school students. Each semester you complete a Chabot application and the concurrent enrollment packet. You can take any class except basic skills and PE.
how_to_apply: Apply to Chabot, pick a class, fill out the IDE Enrollment Form, then register through MyPortal. Questions: Admissions & Records, 510-723-6701.
notes: Also offers CCAP classes at your high school and a Summer Academy. Middle schoolers have a separate Bridge to College program.
duration: Per term
pay_detail: Enrollment fees are waived. Out-of-state and international students pay $370 per unit. You buy your own books and arrange your own transportation. Maximum 11 units.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page encourages students of all backgrounds to apply, especially Oakland public and charter school students. No skills, experience or GPA is needed. Admission is competitive: an initial review, then an information session for applicants and families. Age and residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Online application from February 1 to March 31, then an initial review and an information session for applicants and families. The page also has an interest survey to get application updates.
notes: Corrected on 2026-10-07 after reading the program's own page. The old chabotspace.org/volunteer/ link now returns 404, so the card points to the Galaxy Explorers page. This is a fee-based program ($1,500 a year tuition) unless the family qualifies for Career Access, which is based on need and census tract data. Floor shifts are 2 per month in the school year and 3 per month in summer. Whether paid Interns need a California work permit is not stated on the page, so we leave the work permit answer blank.
duration: 3 years (summer before 10th grade through 12th grade)
pay_detail: Annual tuition is $1,500 per student (one payment by June 1, or $750 by June 1 and $750 by September 1). The need-based Career Access program covers tuition and adds a stipend. 12th-grade Interns receive a stipend.

who_can_apply: The CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers; the East Sacramento post page snippet says ages 15 to 21.
how_to_apply: See the CHP Explorer post locator and contact the East Sacramento post.
notes: The CHP site blocked WebFetch (403) and a browser tab loaded blank, so ages come from search results and are unconfirmed. CHP has other posts. Confirm age limits and meeting times with the post. See also California Highway Patrol Explorer Program for the statewide competition. Ages differ by source: the CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers, while the post page snippet says 15 to 21. Re-checked on 2026-10-09: the CHP post page returned HTTP 403 again, so it could not be read and the card stays snippet-only.

who_can_apply: There is a separate application for ages 16 to 17. Animal care and docent roles are 18 and up. Animal care also needs 100 hours of earlier volunteering.
how_to_apply: Submit the 16-17 volunteer application. Then go to the next orientation. They tell you about it by email.
notes: The center does not take court-ordered community service right now. If you have questions, write to volunteers@thelivingcoast.org.
duration: Ongoing, based on availability. In animal care, 3 absences within 60 days may result in losing your spot.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 to 18 (the page is titled 'Become a Cadet (Ages 12-18)'). The page says your local squadron can answer eligibility questions.
how_to_apply: Find a local squadron. Contact it and visit with a parent. Go to about three meetings. Then apply. You can apply online if your squadron commander says you are eligible, or by mail or fax. Contact: pao@cawgcap.org.
notes: Prices on the California Wing cost page are from 2021 and 2022. Ask your squadron for current amounts. The Northern California Bay Area squadrons are listed on the wing site. The cost page says you must go to encampment to advance to Cadet Second Lieutenant.
duration: Ongoing; weekly squadron meetings
pay_detail: Dues plus uniforms. The cost page (2021 and 2022 figures) lists $45 national dues, $25 squadron dues (can be waived for hardship), and about $205 to $300 total to join with uniforms. Encampment was $300 in 2021, with financial help available. No 2026 figures are posted, so check the National site for current dues.

who_can_apply: High school students at participating schools in 14 counties, including Sacramento and Yolo. Ask the FARMS coordinator at your school.
how_to_apply: Ask your ag or science teacher whether your school participates. Contact Mindy Cunha at mindy@landbasedlearning.org.
notes: Advanced FARMS tier (year-long research, job shadowing) also exists. Main office (530) 795-1520. CLBL headquarters is The Maples Farm in Woodland.
duration: school year, 6+ field days
pay_detail: No cost or stipend listed on the page.

who_can_apply: Students at Luther Burbank High, Grant Union High and Sacramento Academic and Vocational Academy (SAVA).
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Ask a teacher or counselor at your host school, or contact the Center for Land-Based Learning: info@landbasedlearning.org or (530) 795-1520.
notes: Only at the three host schools. Grant Union students can earn college credit through a Sacramento State partnership (ACE program). Pay rate and hours per week are not posted. Paid job for a minor, so a work permit is likely needed.
duration: year-long
pay_detail: Pay rate not posted on the page.

who_can_apply: Concurrent enrollment: high school students in grades 9 to 12. Dual enrollment: students at CSM's partner high schools; talk to your school counselor.
how_to_apply: Create an OpenCCC account and apply to CSM online. For dual enrollment, meet with your high school counselor first, then register with the Dual Enrollment team. Questions: csmoutreach@smccd.edu.
notes: Dual enrollment is only through CSM's partner high schools. Concurrent enrollment is open to any high schooler but may need your counselor's approval at some schools. Skyline and Canada colleges run similar programs (not checked here).
pay_detail: Free. Dual enrollment includes textbooks and materials; concurrent enrollment is free for up to 11 units per semester.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the CHM internships page to join the mailing list.
notes: CHM says it is not accepting Teen Program applications right now; the page gives no reopening date. Join the interest list to be told when it opens. Pay and length are not stated.
duration: Not stated on the page
pay_detail: Not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Students at West Contra Costa USD, Leadership Public Schools, Griffin Technology Academies, or Middle College High School on campus. Requirements vary by school.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor. Questions: earlycollegecredit@contracosta.edu.
notes: Serves West Contra Costa County (Richmond, San Pablo). No deadlines are listed on the page.
duration: Per term
pay_detail: Free: no tuition, textbook or enrollment fees.

who_can_apply: Summer Read: entering 8th grade or above, with parent consent. Computer Docent and Homework Help: age 16 or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer interest form on ccclib.org/volunteer. You may be called for an interview. Forms stay on file for six months.
notes: Contact your branch to see if it is taking volunteers now.
duration: Summer Read 1 to 2 hours a week; Computer Docents at least 2 hours a week

who_can_apply: California high school students completing grades 8 to 12. Non-California residents and international students cannot apply. Selected on academic strength and interest in math and science. You pick one campus and cluster choices.
how_to_apply: Online application plus teacher recommendations and parent signature. Pay the application fee. If accepted, pay one-third by Apr 7, 2027 and the rest by Apr 16, 2027.
notes: Competitive. Residential, so you live on campus for four weeks. Financial aid is reviewed separately from admission and needs a parent income document; it has a hard deadline. Program session dates are listed as TBA. Pick UC Davis as your campus on the application. COSMOS runs on several UC campuses (UC Davis, UC Irvine, UC San Diego and UC Santa Cruz); this card is the Davis campus. See the UC COSMOS site for the others: https://jacobs.ucsd.edu/cosmos. The dates page lists the application fee as both $48 and $46, so confirm the amount before paying.
duration: about 4 weeks (2027 dates TBA)
pay_detail: Program cost $5,793 (2027 page), plus $48 application fee and a 2.5% card fee. Financial aid is available for admitted students with need, but not guaranteed.

who_can_apply: Students who have finished 8th grade. A parent must send a one-time consent form. Your high school principal signs the concurrent form.
how_to_apply: Apply online to OCC. Pick "Enrolling in High School and College at the same time." Then your parent sends in the consent form. You email the signed Concurrent Enrollment Form to dualenrollment@occ.cccd.edu. Only handwritten signatures count.
notes: The one-time parent consent form is also honored at Golden West College and Coastline College. After you graduate you must re-apply as a first-time college student. Help: fpr@occ.cccd.edu.
duration: By term. Up to 11 units in fall or spring, 10 in summer, 3 in winter.
pay_detail: Per-unit enrollment fees are waived. Concurrent students pay the College Service, Student Health and Student Representation fees plus books and supplies. CCAP classes at high schools may only need textbooks.

who_can_apply: The page does not state a minimum age. Ask the department before you apply, because lifeguard jobs and leader jobs often have different age rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the city's Parks and Community Services employment page.
notes: The city also runs free after-school teen centers for grades 7 to 12 and a Summer Teen Camp for grades 7 to 10, which are programs to attend, not jobs. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Part time, 8 to 30 hours a week
pay_detail: The page says all positions start at $20 an hour. That page was last updated May 11, 2023, and no 2026 rate is posted there, so confirm the current rate.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 (two separate groups).
how_to_apply: Use the Register HERE link for your committee on the Teen Committees page (cosumnescsd.gov/460/Teen-Committees). Questions: call The Grove Teen Center at 916-405-5622 or email thegrove@Cosumnescsd.gov.
notes: Meeting times, location and deadlines are not posted on the page, so ask the District. Other volunteer roles on that page (adaptive recreation, youth coaching) are 18 and older.
duration: One school year. Teen Action Academy runs September to June; Teen Leadership Committee runs August to May. Meets every other week.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18, high school juniors and seniors, 2.0 GPA, and a physician-completed medical exam form.
how_to_apply: Email explorers@cosumnescsd.gov to get application details. Fire Admin phone: 916-405-7100.
notes: Serves the Elk Grove area. Needs a physician-completed medical exam form. Meeting schedule and any costs are not posted on the page.
duration: School year

who_can_apply: Ages 16 and older. Some departments accept only people 18 and older. Junior volunteers under 18 need a signed parental consent form.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, then an in-person interview and a health screening. The background check applies to adults only. Questions go to cpmcvolunteer@sutterhealth.org.
notes: Read on the official Sutter Health listing 2026-10-07. Not stated on the listing: TB test or immunization requirements, application window, and pay (unpaid volunteer role). The health screening is required but its contents are not described on this listing. Sutter's separate CPMC student volunteer page could not be read from this environment, so no details from it are used here. The listing is a lobby role, so it fits teens 16 and older who want to try hospital volunteering; it is not a high school program.
duration: Minimum 100 hours in one year, at least three to four hours per week
pay_detail: Volunteer role; no pay stated on the listing

who_can_apply: California residents in grades 8 to 12. Up to 20 students from out of state and other countries may also be enrolled. Each department has its own assignments.
how_to_apply: Apply online by department. A full application has the form and two teacher references, not peers. It has an unofficial transcript and department assignments. It has the $20 fee. It has the financial aid request if you want aid. Students can apply to more than one department. Each needs a full application.
notes: Students who finish can get 3 units of college extension credit from the California State University system (per the FAQ). Not a job. The pages did not name the 2027 campus, so check before planning travel.
duration: About one month: first day of classes July 5 and graduation July 31, 2027
pay_detail: Tuition and fees for California residents were $5,174 for 2026; 2027 rates 'will be posted soon'. Need based aid is available to California residents (nearly half of past students had much of tuition covered). $20 application fee, with fee waivers for students with financial need.

who_can_apply: Cupertino residents who are in 7th to 10th grade now. The city page says seniors are not eligible to apply.
how_to_apply: When recruitment is open, use the 'Apply to be a Teen Commissioner' form on the city page. The page also links a supplemental questions list. Questions about applications go to cityclerk@cupertino.gov.
notes: Meets monthly, September through May, at 6 p.m. on the second Wednesday. It meets in the Quinlan Community Center Conference Room (10185 North Stelling Road), with a teleconference option. Commission email teencommission@cupertino.gov. Staff liaison Sonya Lee, Recreation Manager, (408) 777-3121. Pay is not mentioned on the page, so it is listed as unpaid. The page says members may be in 12th grade during their term. The 8th-to-11th rule applies to applicants.
duration: Two-year staggered terms

who_can_apply: Lifeguard Training: you must turn 15 by the last day of the course. Junior Lifeguarding: pass a swim skills check on day one (25 yards of front crawl and breaststroke, tread water 1 minute, and more). Junior Swim Instructor: no age or swim test listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Register for a course through City of Davis online registration (the page links to it). Questions: 530-757-5626 or csweb@cityofdavis.org.
notes: Training can lead to City of Davis aquatics work. Junior Swim Instructor is for teens who may want to work for Davis Aquatics later, with volunteer chances after the training. The page does not promise a job. Lifeguard certification needs full attendance and passing tests. Job minimum ages are set in each posting at cityofdavis.org/jobs.
duration: varies by course
pay_detail: Course fees apply. Amounts are not on the page; check the Rec Guide or online registration.

who_can_apply: Age 15 or older to officiate or keep score, and 16 or older to coach. You need CPR and First Aid certification before the season starts and a working knowledge of basketball rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the City of Davis job page (NEOGOV). Applicants are screened on experience and may be interviewed.
notes: Temporary part-time with no benefits. Games are Saturdays at the Davis High School community gyms. Other City of Davis seasonal postings such as Parks Maintenance Aide (18 and older) and Pool Maintenance Aide (21 and older) are not open to teens.
duration: 6-week season starting the week of January 18, 2027
pay_detail: $17.39 an hour

who_can_apply: DJUSD high school students. The page does not list which schools offer which pathway. Ask your counselor.
how_to_apply: Contact your school counselor to enroll in a CTE course. Internships are on the Student Internships tab. See the Internship and Career Development Course.
notes: Page does not say which schools offer which pathways, or give grade or age rules. DJUSD office: (530) 757-5300. Related: the Internship and Career Development Course and the Summer Apprenticeship.
pay_detail: School classes, no pay. Course credit.

who_can_apply: Davis teens ages 14 to 17. Up to 24 members. Needs a full school-year commitment.
how_to_apply: Fill out the TLC application on the Teens page. Questions: Micayla Valceschini, mvalceschini@cityofdavis.org.
notes: Meetings are at the Veterans Memorial Center, 203 E. 14th St. Up to 24 teens, and it is a full school-year commitment. The application closed Oct 2, so ask the city whether late applicants can still join.
duration: Oct 13, 2026 to May 18, 2027, meets 2nd and 4th Tuesdays, 7:00 to 8:30 pm

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in any California high school, grades 9 to 12 (rising 9th graders included). Needs permission from a parent or guardian and your school principal. No GPA requirement.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor, apply for admission, set up MyPortal, finish the Dual Enrollment overview, check prerequisites, submit the school permission form, then register. Questions: outreach@deanza.edu.
notes: Math and English classes need an assessment (usually based on your school transcript). Students can buy a VTA SmartPass for unlimited bus and light rail rides. Undocumented students can take part. Parents cannot see your college records without your written consent.
duration: Quarter system (fall, winter, spring, summer); a standard class is 12 weeks
pay_detail: No enrollment fees for up to 11 units a quarter (De Anza and Foothill combined). You still pay for textbooks in most courses and may pay other fees.

who_can_apply: High school students join through a school chapter and its advisor, or a school can start a chapter. Contact the DECA advisor at your school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school for a DECA advisor. DECA lists an Online Membership System for joining.
notes: DECA says it has about 317,600 high school members in 4,510 chapters. Not every school has a chapter. California-specific details were not on the page.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages. Ask your advisor for chapter dues and conference fees.

who_can_apply: Teen volunteers, around age 15 and up. The page says a 14-year-old may start the application one month before their 15th birthday. The page does not state a maximum age.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application for a role. The roles are Exhibit Host, Team Spark and Team Celebration. Email a resume and a letter from an adult who is not family. Send them to VolunteerLA@discoverycube.org. Then do an interview and a mandatory orientation.
notes: The museum is in Sylmar in the San Fernando Valley. The letter of recommendation cannot come from a family member. Questions: 818-686-2835.
duration: Minimum 60 hours; two 4-hour shifts every 30 days
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: The page gives one age rule: if you are 14, you may start the application process one month before your 15th birthday. No grade level is stated.
how_to_apply: Online application form, a resume, a letter of recommendation, then an interview. The full application must be in before an interview is scheduled.
notes: Plan for the 60-hour minimum if you need service hours that are checked. Location: 2500 N Main Street, Santa Ana, CA 92705. Questions: volunteeroc@discoverycube.org.
duration: At least one four-hour shift every 30 days. 60 hours of service before the Cube verifies your hours.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page lists no fees.

who_can_apply: Davis Joint Unified high school students. Some sites have priority rules (Dignity Health for Patient Care pathway students; Ford ACE for Transportation pathway students).
how_to_apply: Talk to your counselor or contact Internship Specialist Alexha Contreras (alcontreras@djusd.net, 530-757-5400 x170).
notes: Many other 2026-27 host sites are listed on the page; some have priority rules (Mercy General: Patient Care pathway students; Ford ACE: Transportation pathway students). Credit needs weekly meetings, an evaluation and a reflection. The page is written for DJUSD students.
pay_detail: Unpaid internships; course credit with evaluation and reflection required.

who_can_apply: Teens entering 7th grade or higher. Complete the online application; staff review it and then tell you how to register. The page lists separate fees for Dublin residents and non-residents.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application when it is open (closed for 2026). Staff review it and then tell you how to register at dublinrecguide.com. Questions: Dublin.Lead@dublin.ca.gov.
notes: This is a fee-based training and volunteer-style program run by the city, not a paid job. Families pay the registration fee; the city page does not say teens are paid. The page does not name a residency rule for applying. Shifts are not pre-assigned; participants pick their own shifts in the registration system.
duration: The 2026 program ran June 8, 2026 to August 7, 2026. Participants are encouraged to help with recreation or aquatics programs for at least two weeks.
pay_detail: Registration fee for the 2026 program: $119 for Dublin residents, $143 for non-residents. No wage is stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Dublin and be enrolled in middle or high school (committee bylaws). The committee has 13 members and 3 alternates; at least 6 members must be high school students.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the city page. Call Parks and Community Services at 925-556-4500 or use the contact link on the committee page to ask when the next recruitment opens.
notes: Meets 7:00 pm, second Wednesday of the month, Dublin Senior Center, 7600 Amador Valley Blvd; July and August meet only as needed. Bylaws say members must stay enrolled in middle or high school, and a member is removed if they stop living in Dublin or stop being enrolled. Older (2020 and 2021) notices mention late-winter recruitment; that is last-cycle information and was not confirmed for 2027. Teens who want a seat should check the city page each spring.
duration: One-year term. The 2026-27 members are listed for June 2026 to May 2027.
pay_detail: Volunteer committee seat. No pay is stated on the city page.

who_can_apply: Not stated.
how_to_apply: The home page has a Sign Up button for volunteers, but the volunteer page it links to showed a 404 error on 2026-10-09. Contact EBAYC directly (offices in Oakland and Sacramento are listed on the home page).
notes: Read the home page on 2026-10-09. It says EBAYC has many volunteer opportunities and welcomes volunteer groups and student internships, but it gives no ages, dates or pay. The volunteer page linked from it (ebayc.org/volunteer/) returned a 404 error on Oct 7 and again on Oct 9, 2026. Confirm the minimum age with EBAYC.

who_can_apply: High school students in the EBMUD service area. For 2026 the East Bay program took students referred by partner groups. The Maintenance track (Stockton) required age 16 by June 24, 2026.
how_to_apply: In 2026 you could not apply to EBMUD directly for the East Bay program. Ask a partner to refer you: ACE Mentor, Biotech Partners, Eden Area ROP, Girls Inc. of Alameda County, Youth UpRising. Email internships@ebmud.com, (510) 287-0710.
notes: Referral only in 2026. Separate Mokelumne programs (Fisheries in Lodi, Ranger in Valley Springs, Maintenance in Stockton) ran in 2026 with rolling review.
duration: 6 weeks, mid-June through August, about 16 hours a week
pay_detail: Paid stipend (amount not posted)

who_can_apply: Gate Attendant (high school pathway): at least 16 and completed 10th grade. Other jobs have their own rules; check each posting.
how_to_apply: Apply on governmentjobs.com/careers/ebparks. HR: (510) 544-2154.
notes: The 16 minimum is from the Gate Attendant page; other roles (for example lifeguard) may differ. The park district says it hires hundreds of seasonal students each year.
duration: Seasonal
pay_detail: Pay is not posted on the youth pages. See each job posting.

who_can_apply: Berkeley residents ages 15 to 24, recruited through Berkeley YouthWorks.
how_to_apply: Apply through the City of Berkeley YouthWorks interest form (the Ecology Center sends you there). Contact alex@ecologycenter.org or 510-697-4808.
notes: Berkeley residents only. YouthWorks asks for an interest form and a 15 to 20 minute interview. Pay rate and exact academy dates are not posted.
duration: 8 weeks (summer) or 12 weeks (spring)
pay_detail: Paid; rate not posted

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors attending high school in the Castro Valley, Hayward, San Leandro or San Lorenzo Unified school districts.
how_to_apply: Ask your home high school counselor to contact the Eden Area ROP career counselor at (510) 293-2973. Main office (510) 293-2900.
notes: Center is at 26316 Hesperian Blvd, Hayward. Cost, pay and ages are not stated on the page. Some pathways are offered only at certain high schools. Students outside the four districts are not listed as eligible. Work-based learning is mentioned (for example in education careers) but no formal internship structure is described.
duration: Classes are held Monday to Friday; course length varies by class
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Any high school student who has finished freshman year.
how_to_apply: The volunteer office takes names in April, according to a November 2025 article. The article gives no form or phone number for the junior program. The hospital main phone is 760-340-3911.
notes: Confirm first: the dates come from a November 2025 article, not a page. The Volunteers page does not mention the junior program, and the number 760-773-1304 appears on it with no label.
duration: One shift a week from June orientation to the end of July
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Qualified students in grades 9 to 12 who can benefit from college classes. No age rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Do the Steps for Dual Enrollment each term you want to register. The steps are listed on a separate page. Call 310-660-3344 or email dualenrollment@elcamino.edu.
notes: Unit limits are not on this page. Dual enrollment uses Remind to post updates for students.
duration: By term
pay_detail: Enrollment fees are waived for dual enrollment students.

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older and done with 8th grade. One-year minimum. Competitive, with limited spots. No summer-only option.
how_to_apply: Attend the annual application seminar, then apply. Info on the El Camino Health junior volunteer page.
notes: Hospital does not offer summer-only or programs shorter than one year. Locations are Mountain View and Los Gatos. Spots are limited (earlier check).
duration: At least 1 year
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program; no cost stated on the page

who_can_apply: Youth appointed by the Mayor with City Council approval (10 voting seats). The page does not list ages or grades. A city factsheet in search results reportedly said ages 13 to 18, grades 7 to 12, but that is unconfirmed. The City tries to balance seats by school and council district.
how_to_apply: When a seat opens, use the Apply to the Youth Commission link (City Clerk vacancies page). Questions: youthcommission@elkgrove.gov or (916) 627-3254.
notes: Age and grade rules were not on the pages, so confirm with the City before applying. Appointed seats, so competitive. Sign up for vacancy emails on elkgrove.gov to hear when a recruitment opens. Re-checked on 2026-10-09: the City page returned HTTP 403, so it could not be read again and the card stays snippet-only.
duration: Meets 2nd Tuesday, Sept to May, 6:00 pm, Elk Grove Council Chambers

who_can_apply: Local teens. The page does not give an age range or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Get the Teen Advisory Board Application (PDF) from the page, or pick one up at the Youth Services Desk on the 2nd floor. The page says to send the completed application to Teen Services by email. The page text did not show the email address, so confirm it before sending.
notes: Phone for the Teen Services Librarian: 760-839-4283 (listed in the card notes; not confirmed on the page text). Page lists no age range or cost.
duration: 2026-2027 school year; meetings on the second Monday of each month, 4:30 to 5:30 p.m.
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14. Volunteers need fingerprinting and a background check. Review Crew and Teen Advisory Board members do not need them. You must have an interview with the Volunteer Coordinator. The library does not accept court-ordered community service.
how_to_apply: Go to the City of Escondido volunteer website. Fill out the application there. You can call or email the City Community Engagement Liaison with questions. The number is 760-839-4523.
notes: Some roles on the page are for adults only. They are shelver, Friends shop and literacy tutor. The Review Crew and Teen Advisory Board do not need fingerprinting or a background check.
duration: A regular schedule is expected
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens on the Review Crew earn 1 community service hour for every 2 qualifying book reviews.

who_can_apply: California students without a high school diploma or GED. You need approval from your school counselor or principal.
how_to_apply: Submit the dual enrollment application, get your high school counselor or principal to approve, then enroll. Counseling: mycounselor@evc.edu, 408-270-6475.
notes: CCAP classes are closed cohort classes held at partner high schools, so ask your school if it has an agreement. The page does not state a grade or age rule. Textbook costs for non-CCAP students are not stated.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: No enrollment fees for dual enrollment students; material fees are waived for CCAP students only

who_can_apply: 11th graders at high schools that EXP supports. The 2025-2026 list includes Carson, Gardena, Lawndale, San Pedro, Phineas Banning and Sato Academy. It also lists some Long Beach schools: Cabrillo, Jordan, Lakewood, Long Beach Poly and Wilson. Some schools in Orange County and Barstow are listed too.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply to the Port directly; placement goes through EXP. Ask your school counselor if your school is an EXP school, or email internship@expfuture.org.
notes: Only for students at partner schools. Phone: 424.368.7100. The Port of Los Angeles Summer Internship (10 weeks, paid) is college students only. The page does not mention work permits.
duration: Port of LA placement is 2 to 6 weeks; other placements not stated
pay_detail: EXP lists 171 paid internships for Summer 2026. The hourly pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: Local high school students. Past interns came from Davis Senior High, Dixon High and Natomas Pacific Pathways Prep.
how_to_apply: No application process is posted. Use the contact page on the Facciotti Lab site to email the lab with a short note about your interests.
notes: Informal opportunity with no posted process, pay, dates or contact on that page. The lab names a partner teacher at Davis Senior High and lists one current intern, so openings may be rare.
pay_detail: Pay not stated. Ask the lab.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15. Space is limited. Register in WebTrac.
how_to_apply: Register through Folsom WebTrac.
notes: Source is the city's May 22, 2026 news post, which does not list a fee or the 2027 dates. Held at Oak Chan Elementary School. Check the Folsom Parks and Recreation site and WebTrac in spring 2027.
duration: 8 weekly sessions (2026: June 8 to July 31, Mon to Fri 8:30 to 4:00)
pay_detail: Fee not stated in the news post.

who_can_apply: Any current high school student in grades 9 to 12. Apply to Foothill, then submit the Special Admit form signed by a parent or guardian and your high school principal or administrator. Meet course prerequisites; talk to your high school counselor.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to Foothill, submit the Special Admit form (parent and principal signatures, plus an unofficial transcript if asked), register, and pay any fees. Admissions: (650) 949-7325.
notes: Foothill can give a free Clipper SmartPass for VTA buses and light rail. Undocumented students are welcome. Grades go on your permanent college record, and your parents cannot see college records. Partner-district options also exist: Middle College, College Now! (MVLA), Firebird Academy (Fremont Union).
duration: One quarter at a time
pay_detail: No cost up to 11 units in a regular quarter (6 in summer), counting Foothill and De Anza together. Textbooks and other fees are not covered.

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older. Those 18 and over also pass a background check and need a valid Social Security number. You commit to 150 hours a year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the PDF application form and email it to the Volunteer Office. Then do an interview, an orientation, two TB tests and a flu shot.
notes: Volunteer Office: (714) 378-7000, Mon to Fri 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Patient Care Pavilion, 18111 Brookhurst St. The application PDF was not checked.
duration: 150 hours per year
pay_detail: Unpaid. If accepted you pay a $25 registration fee.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page says all Fremont high school students are welcome.
how_to_apply: Go to the volunteer portal page. Click Fill in an application. If you already volunteer through MyImpactPage.com, log in. Questions: ebuchanan@aclibrary.org.
notes: Some events in the community need extra forms. They also have a separate sign up.
duration: Tuesdays 4:00 to 6:00 p.m. (October 13, 20 and 27, 2026 listed)

who_can_apply: High school students in the Fremont, New Haven or Newark school districts. Charter, home school and independent study students should call to ask about the price.
how_to_apply: Sign up during pre-registration at your home school. Ask your school counselor, College and Career Specialist or Career Center for help with scheduling. Buses take students to and from the ROP center.
notes: Center is at 5019 Stevenson Blvd, Fremont. Phone (510) 657-1865. College credit partners named on the site: Chabot, Las Positas, Mission, Ohlone and Universal Technical Institute. Grade levels are not stated on the pages. The site's jobs page for high schoolers only links to Indeed and a company careers page.
pay_detail: Free for students in those three districts.

who_can_apply: Age 14 and up. Teens aged 14 and 15 must come with an adult who also registers as a volunteer. Under 14 is not accepted.
how_to_apply: Create an account at volunteer.tcvfoodbank.org, sign the Volunteer Handbook and Consent forms, then sign up for shifts. Email volunteer@tcvfoodbank.org or call 510-598-4066.
notes: TCV does not sign court or traffic ticket hours. The page did not say whether school service hours are signed, so ask. Orientation was not mentioned on this page.

who_can_apply: Students at Fremont Unified middle and high schools. The page says limited English is not a barrier to joining career and technical education programs.
how_to_apply: The page gives no sign-up steps. Ask your school counselor or principal, or contact Leslie Heller, Director of Secondary Education, (510) 659-2513.
notes: The page is general. It lists 15 industry sectors and 58 career pathways. It does not list internship partners or work-based learning. Ask your counselor which pathways your school offers.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page

who_can_apply: The page does not state ages, grades or residency rules. Ask the Recreation Division.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Call the Recreation Division at 510-494-4300.
notes: Meets 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. on the first Monday of each month except July and August, at City Hall, 3300 Capitol Ave. The page lists 12 members.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the VolunTeens Application linked on the zoo's support page. Group questions: volunteer@fcz.org.
notes: Fresno is in the Central Valley, outside Merced County. The page uses one application link for both VolunTeens and the junior camp counselor role.
duration: Year-round; 1-day training
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Jr. Camp Counselor Application linked on the zoo's support page.
notes: Listed on the zoo's volunteer page; pay is not stated. Fresno is in the Central Valley, outside Merced County.
duration: Summer camp weeks; hours not stated
pay_detail: Not stated; listed on the zoo's volunteer page.

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Attend a Teen Advisory Board meeting or submit a book review. The page does not describe a sign-up form. Allow up to 7 business days after an activity for your credit to show. Call (714) 773-5719.
notes: Easy way to start earning service hours. The Teen Advisory Board page on the same site has more detail; it was not read.
duration: Board meets on the first and third Tuesday of each month at 6 p.m. (starting Sept 1, 2026)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns volunteer service hours (1 hour per meeting or approved review).

who_can_apply: High school students age 15 and over. The hospital picks based on your application. It looks at whether you can keep the weekly commitment. It also looks at your school background and career interests. There is no job shadowing or internship.
how_to_apply: When applications open, contact St. Jude volunteer services at Stjudevolunteers@providence.org or 714-992-3000 ext. 2878. Questions should come from the student. Accepted volunteers must go to an orientation and get a health screening. This takes about one month in all.
notes: Questions: Stjudevolunteers@providence.org or 714-992-3000 ext. 2878. Questions should come from the student. Health screening and orientation are required (about one month).
duration: Minimum one year and 140 hours a year. Shifts: Mon to Fri 4 to 7 p.m. or weekends 8 a.m. to 9 p.m.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Motivated rising high school seniors enrolled at a Genesys Works partner school. The Bay Area page says 100% of its students qualify for free or reduced lunch. No GPA is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, then interview if accepted, then get summer training details. Phone 415-442-0280, email gwba@ba.genesysworks.org.
notes: You must attend a partner school, and the lists of schools and counties were not on the pages. Ask them whether your school is a partner. No 2027 dates or deadline are posted. Interns work for pay, so a California work permit applies if you are under 18.
duration: 8 weeks of training, then a school-year internship
pay_detail: Paid internship; hourly rate not posted (the page only lists total interns' wages)

who_can_apply: Sophomores and juniors currently enrolled in high school in Los Angeles County, who are at least 16 when the program starts and live within 25 miles of the Getty Center.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window opens in early February. Questions: gettyteens@getty.edu.
notes: Supported by the Vera R. Campbell Foundation. The page calls it a paid summer internship but says only that interns receive a stipend. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Mid-June to early August; interns commit to all program days
pay_detail: Every intern gets a stipend after finishing the program. Amount not stated. Lunch and transportation to the Getty sites are provided.

who_can_apply: Girls and young women in grades 9 to 12. Programs run at the Simpson Center in Oakland (year-round) and Cal State East Bay in Hayward (summer).
how_to_apply: Use the Contact Us page at girlsinc-alameda.org. Office: 510 16th St, Oakland. The site does not list application steps.
notes: The page checked on 2026-10-10 does not mention Code the Game, a fall offering, or grades 10 to 12 for coding. Internship pay, hours and ages are not posted.
pay_detail: Programs are free to families; internships are paid (rate not posted)

who_can_apply: Current high school students. Dual Enrollment: students in Glendale Unified (GUSD) and Burbank Unified (BUSD) taking courses on the class offerings list. Jump Start: everyone else, for college credit only.
how_to_apply: Apply at OpenCCCApply. Then send the Annual Digital Form signed by a parent and your counselor. Find classes, clear any prerequisites and register in MyGCC. Email dual@glendale.edu or call (818) 240-1000 ext. 4767.
notes: Jump Start credit is not guaranteed to count toward high school graduation. A weekly Zoom help hour runs Tuesdays 3:30 to 5:00 PM.
duration: By term
pay_detail: Costs and fee waivers are not stated on the page. Ask dual@glendale.edu.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21 and in school. You have a disability or health condition, such as an IEP, 504 plan, ADHD or anxiety.
how_to_apply: One online Apply Now form covers all GYA programs. A case worker contacts you in 3 to 5 business days. STEP contacts: (818) 937-8005 or (818) 937-8057.
notes: The GYA page does not mention work permits or income rules.
duration: 120 hours
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The hourly rate is not listed.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24. The page lists it as a first job or summer job program. GYA serves youth from Glendale, Burbank and La Canada-Flintridge and the greater Los Angeles County area.
how_to_apply: One online Apply Now form covers all GYA programs. A case worker contacts you in 3 to 5 business days. Office: 1255 S Central Ave, Glendale; (818) 937-8073, Mon to Fri 8 to 5.
notes: The page does not give the hourly rate or weekly hours, so ask the office. The GYA page does not mention work permits. Checked 2026-10-10: the page says one Apply Now form covers all programs and lists no dates, so we cannot tell if summer spots are open now. Left unconfirmed.
duration: Not stated on the page
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The hourly rate is not listed.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21 and low income. GYA serves Glendale, Burbank, La Canada-Flintridge and the greater Los Angeles County area.
how_to_apply: One online Apply Now form covers all GYA programs. A case worker contacts you in 3 to 5 business days. Contact for TEAM: (818) 937-8006.
notes: Income limits and funding sources are not spelled out on the page checked 2026-10-10.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated whether TEAM itself pays. GYA says its other youth programs include paid work experience.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18 by the first day of class. You must volunteer, since you cannot be forced. You must be credit deficient or at risk of dropping out. You must be a U.S. citizen or legal resident and a California resident. You must be clear of felony charges. You must live in one of these places: Santa Cruz, Santa Clara, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Monterey, San Benito, Kings, Tulare, Inyo, San Luis Obispo, Kern, Santa Barbara or Ventura County, or in Lancaster or Palmdale.
how_to_apply: Make sure you meet the rules to apply. Fill out the Interest Form on the site. Then watch the required virtual orientation video. It is a must for the application.
notes: Meant for teens who dropped out or are at risk of dropping out. The FAQ says each ChalleNGe program runs its own admissions. Call or write the academy (contact page on its site) about county rules. Many cadets can earn a GED during the residential phase (FAQ). Some counties on the site have no separate region tag in this guide. They are Santa Cruz, Madera, Fresno, Monterey, San Benito, Kings, Tulare, Inyo, San Luis Obispo, Kern and Ventura. Lancaster and Palmdale are in Los Angeles County.
duration: The page states a 17 1/2 month residential program. The length of the follow-up phase is not stated on this page; ask the academy.
pay_detail: Free to participants (the site says offered free of charge, paid by federal and state partnerships).

who_can_apply: Age 16 and up for construction sites, even with a parent or guardian. Ages 16 to 18 bring a signed minor waiver. Age 15 and under can help with fundraising, flyers or lunch for site volunteers.
how_to_apply: The page gives no online sign-up link; there is usually a volunteer kiosk on site. Call 866-450-4432 or email Volunteer@HabitatEBSV.org. Groups of 5 or more use the group pages.
notes: Hands-on building experience for age 16 and up. Specific build sites were not listed on the page; ask which are near you.
pay_detail: No volunteer fee mentioned on the page

who_can_apply: At least 16 to volunteer on a job site. The page lists no age minimum for the ReStore and no special rules for 16 and 17 year olds. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Make a VolunteerHub account (sachabitat.volunteerhub.com), register for and attend a one hour HabiTour orientation, then sign up for shifts. Email volunteers@habitatgreatersac.org or call (916) 440-1215.
notes: Ask whether under-18 volunteers need a parent signature or waiver, since the page does not say. Group volunteering contact: gcabral@habitatgreatersac.org. Office: 819 North 10th St, Sacramento.
duration: Shifts Tue to Sat (times not listed)

who_can_apply: Monthly projects: filter the calendar by age to see which are open to you. HandsOn Tomorrow and the Youth Volunteer Council are for Bay Area high school students; the Council requires finishing HandsOn Tomorrow first.
how_to_apply: Use the Community Calendar at handsonbayarea.org/calendar and filter by age. Email info@handsonbayarea.org or call 415-541-9616.
notes: HandsOn Tomorrow, a 2-week summer program (up to 40 hours), will not be running in summer 2026. The page does not say when it returns and does not use the word paused. The Youth Volunteer Council needs HandsOn Tomorrow first, so for now the monthly calendar projects are the way in. Age limits vary by project.
duration: Monthly projects; HandsOn Tomorrow was 2 weeks
pay_detail: No cost or pay stated on the pages

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. Animal handling, public speaking or working-with-children experience helps. It is not required.
how_to_apply: Download the volunteer application, write a 1-page cover letter about your interests and goals, and send both by mail, email, fax or in person to 1300 Senter Road, San Jose. Selected applicants interview. Phone (408) 794-6425.
notes: Minimum 48 hours a year (about 4 hours a month). Not everyone is picked, but you can reapply the next season.
duration: At least 48 hours a year (about 4 hours a month)
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated on the page

who_can_apply: The page says ambitious high school students, including rising juniors, may enroll. No age range or grade rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page of the Summer Session site. You send a registration application with a transcript and pay fees before the course starts.
notes: Costs money and the courses are college level. Check the site in winter for 2027 dates and prices.
duration: 2026 Session I began May 26 and Session II began June 15
pay_detail: Tuition is $4,250 per 3-credit course and $5,000 per 4-credit course (2026 prices). Financial aid on the page is only for Harvey Mudd students.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 and up. Some jobs have their own age rules, listed on each opportunity. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the volunteer agreement.
how_to_apply: Create a volunteer profile, then register for a one-time event or submit an interest form for a service project. Service projects need a background check and TB risk assessment before starting.
notes: This page lists many volunteer roles, not one program, so each role's own age rule applies. Verification of service hours is emailed on request. Volunteers with court orders should follow the district process (info@haywardrec.org).
duration: One-time events, or service projects that run 6 months or longer.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. Library service hours cannot be used for community service required by a judge or court.
how_to_apply: Use the APPLY TO VOLUNTEER online interest form linked from the library page. Questions go to hpl.teens@hayward-ca.gov.
notes: The page says the roles are subject to change, so check the online interest form for current openings. The Just for Teens page describes its events for grades 9-12, while the volunteer page says ages 13-17; the volunteer page is the one used here. An older 2023 city notice describes a monthly Teen Advisory Group meeting (1st Wednesday, Downtown Library, ages 13-17, no commitment). That notice was not re-checked for 2026, so ask hpl.teens@hayward-ca.gov whether it still meets.
duration: Flexible. Volunteers sign up for 1-hour shifts.

who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 20 who live in the City of Hayward or within the Hayward Unified School District boundaries. Applicants under 18 need a parent or guardian consent form.
how_to_apply: Get the application and the Parent Agreement and Contact Information form from the City of Hayward website, or call the City Clerk at (510) 583-4400, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays. Applicants are interviewed by a panel.
notes: The official Youth Commission page returned 404. The newest notice read is from April 2025. The 2021 notice said meetings were on the first and third Mondays, so the meeting schedule may have changed. Confirm the 2026 cycle with the City Clerk before applying.
duration: Meetings at Hayward City Hall, September to June (meeting day not confirmed; the 2021 notice said first and third Mondays). The 2021 notice said two-year terms.

who_can_apply: Black male students entering grades 9, 10 or 11. No coding experience needed. Must commit to the full 15 months.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Immersion Program page on hiddengeniusproject.org.
notes: The apply page says OUR 2027 APPLICATION IS NOW OPEN and lists no closing date. The immersion page still shows the old Feb 21, 2025 deadline. The immersion page lists Oakland and Richmond among its sites.
duration: 15 months
pay_detail: Free to join; no stipend listed

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. Application, interview, orientation and hands-on training.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Flight Teen application online, then expect a call to schedule an interview, attend volunteer orientation, and train with an active volunteer.
notes: Year-round, ongoing applications. Weekend shifts only. Interview timing and training length are not stated.
duration: Alternating Saturdays or Sundays (1st and 3rd, or 2nd and 4th), plus an extra shift on a 5th weekend some months
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated on the page

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 living in the City of Los Angeles. The checklist PDF (2024 version) lists the other rules on who can join. Check the current one.
how_to_apply: Create an application on the Hire LA site, then bring or upload proof of age, right-to-work (I-9) documents, City of LA residency and the family income form.
notes: Cycle dates are not confirmed, so check with EWDD before you count on a summer 2027 spot. The home page Youth section says ages 14 to 30. That does not match the 14 to 24 overview used here, so check the current age range. The same city department runs 14 free YouthSource Centers for ages 14 to 24. They offer school help, job readiness and some paid internships. Ask at your nearest center, for example Boyle Heights 323-526-5800 or South LA 323-903-6926. Under 18 you need a California work permit. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps. Checked 2026-10-10: the home page still says "Accepting Applications for" with no year or dates, so left unconfirmed.
duration: Varies. Student to Student Success is up to 140 hours in one school semester (20 hours of training, up to 120 hours of service).
pay_detail: Paid. The home page does not state an hourly rate.

who_can_apply: Local students ages 16 to 18. No grade level is stated.
how_to_apply: The page lists no application or interest form for this program. Call the Volunteer Office to ask when interest will be taken again.
notes: Not offered: summer, short-term, hands-on patient care, shadowing or observation. Volunteer Office phones: Newport Beach (949) 764-8264, Irvine (949) 517-3152. The page does not state the weekly hours.
duration: Not stated
