notes: The page prints 2025 in a few date lines for the 2026 program, so check dates on the page. The Playhouse has a form to get a note when 2027 applications post.
duration: 9 days (Junior) or 15 weekdays (Conservatory)
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $500 for Junior Conservatory, $850 for Conservatory. A scholarship application is offered.

who_can_apply: Any San Diego high school student who is a rising 10th to 12th grader.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen Council application form during the open window. Applicants were told the result by Sept 18 in 2026.
notes: The page still says applications are now open, but its own deadline of Sept 4, 2026 has passed. Questions: Gia Battista Figueroa (email on the page).
duration: One school year (2026/27 first Teen Council meeting is listed for Oct 12, 2026)
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: See the museum's main volunteer page and Volunteer Application link, or contact the museum at 619-232-3821.
notes: The page gives no application steps beyond pointing to the volunteer application. Ask the museum about the time commitment.
duration: Summer camp season; exact dates not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page says you gain work experience and/or college credit.

who_can_apply: High school students with approval from their high school district and a parent or guardian. Students under 16 also need each instructor to sign an Under 16 form. Home-schooled students need extra forms.
how_to_apply: Get approval from your high school district and a parent. Apply online to Palomar. Fill out the K12 Special Admission Approval Form. Turn it in at Enrollment Services or email it to admissions@palomar.edu.
notes: Part-time (11 units or fewer) enrollment fee is waived. Everyone pays the mandatory Health Fee and Student Center Fee. The same page lists GEAR UP, Upward Bound and Educational Talent Search for some North County schools.
duration: Up to 7 units in fall or spring and 5 units in summer without a petition
pay_detail: The $46 per unit tuition is waived for concurrent enrollment. You pay for books and some fees. Dual enrollment at partner high schools is free.

who_can_apply: Junior volunteers are 16 and 17 years old. A parent or guardian must come to the interview, orientation and TB test. You give a school counselor contact.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Junior Volunteer application online. A parent or guardian must attend the interview, orientation and TB test. Give a school counselor or advisor contact. Screening can take up to six weeks.
notes: The processing fee pays part of the TB screen and background check. It also pays for uniforms and badge parts. You can volunteer at one site at a time, so pick Poway or Escondido, not both. Volunteers in good standing can ask for a letter of recommendation.
duration: 100 hours minimum. Juniors can do one 4-hour shift every other week.
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is a one-time processing fee; the amount is not on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Minimum age is 13. Under 13 must come with an adult. Volunteers (including 13 to 17 year olds) who work with minors, seniors or people with disabilities must be fingerprinted and cleared by state law.
how_to_apply: Register on the volunteer sign-up page, then pick events or roles. Fingerprinting is by appointment (619-236-6686) for roles that need it. Wear closed-toe shoes and bring water, a hat and sunscreen.
notes: Not every role needs fingerprints. The page lists Tecolote Nature Center and Tri-Canyon among its chances.
duration: One-time events or regular roles
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21. You pass a 20 question multiple choice test and a background check. Then you interview with a Police Sergeant and two Cadets.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Then go to a recruiting meeting at Police Plaza (4020 Murphy Canyon Rd). Bring a government photo ID. The meeting can last up to three hours. It includes a 20 question test.
notes: The activities page describes some activities. One is minor decoy work with detectives. A parent should read the page. You must finish the Cadet Academy first. Then you can become a cadet.
duration: Ongoing. You finish a Cadet Academy first. Then there are two meetings a month at Police Plaza: a general meeting on the first Tuesday and a training session on the third Tuesday.
pay_detail: Described as a voluntary position

who_can_apply: Teenagers only. The library's general volunteer rule is that volunteers must be at least 13. Annual volunteer training is required.
how_to_apply: Open the library volunteer opportunities link, pick the Teen Team Program Assistant listing, click the information icon, then 'Fill in an Application'. Sign in or create a MyImpact account and submit. If your branch has no listing, email LibraryVolunteer@sandiego.gov.
notes: Applies to City of San Diego library branches only. San Diego County Library is a different system (see the Teen Service Learner card). The page does not say how many hours a week. Background check and mandated reporter training are listed only for volunteers 18 and older.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Students who go to school in San Diego County and will be the first in their family to graduate from a four-year college. Applicants must be eligible for free or reduced lunch and/or be considered low income. You must meet the program entry rules and reapply each year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. You get a confirmation email and staff follow up with next steps.
notes: This is a college-prep program, not a job. It is a good fit for a teen who wants help planning for college and careers. First-generation means neither parent or guardian has a four-year U.S. degree.
duration: 3 or more hours a week after school
pay_detail: Free for students and families. Not a paid program.

who_can_apply: Southern California residents in grade 10, 11 or 12 who have finished a semester of high school. You are 16 by June 15 and have a 3.0 GPA or higher. You are college bound. You must come to the final poster session.
how_to_apply: Apply online (free). Mentors read applications and interview students. If you accept, you get a registration link and pay by the end of May unless you get a scholarship.
notes: The page calls it a volunteer internship. Pick project prerequisites carefully. Students may do only one REHS internship per summer. 2027 dates are not posted, so check the page in early 2027.
duration: 8 weeks, 10 to 20 hours a week (2026 ran June 8 to July 31)
pay_detail: Free to apply. Registration fee is $2,000 if accepted. Full and partial scholarships are available based on need.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 11 who are at least 14, with a 3.0 GPA or higher and a written recommendation from a school counselor. The page says it is not accepting the class of 2028 now.
how_to_apply: Download and print the junior volunteer form. Fill it out and mail it to Volunteer Services. Then go to a 30 minute interview and a 2 hour orientation with a parent or guardian. You also do a TB test and health screening.
notes: The page takes applications only from grades 9 to 11. It says it is no longer accepting the high school class of 2028. Call 619-740-4175 for junior volunteer information (the page gives this number for that). The mail address is on the page (Volunteer Services, Sharp Grossmont Hospital, PO Box 158, La Mesa, CA 91944).
duration: At least 1 year, one shift a week or two a month
pay_detail: Unpaid. You buy a uniform shirt for a small cost.

who_can_apply: The page has a separate high school student application. The minimum age and any GPA rule are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: When the form opens, submit it. Then go to an in-person info session at Sharp Memorial. After that there is an interview. Onboarding includes a background check and health clearances.
notes: Health clearances include MMR, chickenpox, Tdap, TB blood test, and flu and COVID vaccine or a declination. Check the page for when high school applications reopen.
duration: At least 1 year and 100 service hours, with 75 percent attendance
pay_detail: Unpaid. Benefits listed include a cafeteria discount, meal credit and free parking.

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 and older. You need two reference responses from people who are not friends or family. You cannot serve where you or a family member has worked.
how_to_apply: Apply online and line up two references. They must be work or school contacts, not friends or family. Then do a virtual interview. Send proof of immunity to measles, mumps, rubella and chickenpox. Also send proof of a yearly flu shot during flu season. Show TB clearance. If you are accepted, UC San Diego Health does the TB screening. Then finish online training and go to an in-person orientation and tour.
notes: You may start 2 to 3 months after applying. Questions: volsvcs@health.ucsd.edu or 619-543-6370. Applications outside the summer window will not be considered for summer-only.
duration: One 4-hour shift a week for at least 100 hours over 6 to 8 months. Summer-only option: about 12 weeks and at least 100 hours.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 who are at least 14 when the program starts. You finish one Tier 1 course before applying for Tier 2.
how_to_apply: Apply online when a term opens. Students are accepted on a rolling basis and pay within 2 weeks of acceptance.
notes: Price for Tier 2 and Tier 3 was not checked. Email precollege@ucsd.edu with questions.
duration: About 7 weeks per course (Fall 2026 Tier 1 ran Sept 22 to Nov 12)
pay_detail: Fall 2026 Tier 1 course cost $2,000 in tuition. Scholarships were listed but closed.

who_can_apply: Free career centers. The page says it has helped thousands of 16 to 24 year olds and states no eligibility age, so ask.
how_to_apply: Complete the online program application (10 to 15 minutes). The team follows up about next steps.
notes: The programs page also lists GenAI, workforce support for in-school youth across San Diego County school systems, and EXCEL for in-school and out-of-school young adults in the South Bay; their ages and dates were not checked. Pay and permit rules for under-18 placements are not stated.
duration: Varies by program
pay_detail: Services are free. Some opportunities include paid training or paid on-the-job work experience; rates are not stated.

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors. The application needs an administrator recommendation, a teacher recommendation (core subjects), a parent questionnaire, a student questionnaire and an unofficial transcript, plus a 504 plan if applicable. The page does not say whether students outside San Jose Unified may apply.
how_to_apply: Deliver the application packet (administrator and teacher recommendations, parent and student questionnaires, unofficial transcript) to the Middle College office, Business Building B-107, San Jose City College. Questions: Lisa Canton, lcanton@sjusd.org, 408-298-2191 ext. 3996.
notes: Re-read the SJCC Middle College page on 2026-10-07. The SJUSD Middle College page it links to (https://www.sjusd.org/our-schools/middle-college/nav/) returns 404, so the district's application steps, deadline and selection rules could not be confirmed. Students are responsible for their own transportation. Students from SJUSD can still play sports and join clubs at their home high schools. Confirm the deadline and whether non-SJUSD students can apply with Lisa Canton before applying.
duration: Junior and senior years (the page does not state a fixed length)
pay_detail: Free college classes (6 to 9 college credits). The page does not state other costs.

who_can_apply: Teens Reach is for ages 13 to 18. You need a strong interest in the library and must go to meetings and join in activities. The library does not list an age for Teen Book Reviewer on its volunteer page, so ask Volunteer Services if you are 12 or younger.
how_to_apply: Teens Reach: find your branch's Teens Reach sign-up on Better Impact (each branch has its own) or ask the branch. Teen Book Reviewer: search for it on Better Impact from the library volunteer page, and attend an orientation (on-site or virtual). Questions: volunteer.sjpl@sjlibrary.org or volunteer@sjlibrary.org, or call Volunteer Services at 408-808-2181.
notes: The volunteer page lists both Teens Reach and Teen Book Reviewer as teen roles, and links Teens Reach to its own page at sjpl.org/teensreach, so this one card covers both. Teens Reach meeting times differ by branch; check your branch's page. TeenHQ is at the King Library, 150 E San Fernando.

who_can_apply: San Jose residents. The paid work experience is for ages 14 to 18 who face barriers to employment. Job help (resumes, job fairs) is open to ages 16 to 29. Free to join.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Youth Application on the San Jose Works page. A staff member contacts you afterward.
notes: Pay rate and placement dates are not posted on the pages. The paid work experience is for youth 14 to 18 with barriers to employment; placement is not guaranteed. The FAQ says job help is free for San Jose residents 16 to 29. Under 18 needs a work permit.
pay_detail: Rate not posted (checked 2026-10-07)

who_can_apply: Youth Advisory Council: ages 13 to 19 who live in a San Jose City Council district. Youth Commission: ages 14 to 20. You must live in the district you represent. The term is two years (up to two terms). It meets 4th Monday at 6:30 p.m.
how_to_apply: The Youth Commission is closed. For the Youth Advisory Council, fill out the District Youth Advisory Application. Some districts are paused, so ask the Youth Commission first. A Youth Commissioner contacts you within about two weeks. You can also email Youthcommission@sanjoseca.gov.
notes: Page is hosted by the library. Some council districts are unavailable or paused. YAC members earn community service hours. Pay not mentioned.
duration: Two-year term

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 9 to 12 who can commit to a regular weekly shift for at least 4 months. You must attend one orientation each school year.
how_to_apply: Apply online, attend an in-person orientation at the Main Library, sign the waiver, and commit to a regular shift. Returning volunteers must use their old MyImpact login.
notes: The page mentions both 2026 and January 2026 timing, so confirm the next cycle with the Teen Librarian. It also says a teen should handle their own emails, because the program is meant to prepare you for a first job.
duration: At least 4 months

who_can_apply: The page does not state ages or grades. Ask the Recreation office.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Call Recreation at 510-577-3462 or email SLRec@SanLeandro.Org.
notes: Meets at 6 p.m. on the first Tuesday of the month at the Marina Community Center, 15301 Wicks Blvd. Events listed for the 2025-2026 term include the MLK Celebration and the Cherry Festival and Parade.

who_can_apply: San Mateo County youth ages 14 to 21 can join. The county summer internship is only for members ages 18 to 21. You must attend a 1 hour job prep workshop before using the job board.
how_to_apply: Register as a student member on jobsforyouth.org, attend the 1 hour job prep workshop, then use the job board. For the internship you also attend a mandatory orientation.
notes: Teens under 18 can use the workshops and job board but not the county internship. Phone 650-599-7215, email jobsforyouth@smcgov.org. Must be a San Mateo County resident for the internship.
duration: County summer internship: June to August, about 8 to 10 weeks, 20 to 40 hours a week
pay_detail: Workshops and job board are free. Twenty $2,000 scholarships each year. Pay for the county summer internship is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. Minimum commitment 6 months or one semester. A free background check is required at 16 and older (takes 3 to 6 weeks).
how_to_apply: Pick a branch and apply for a role on Better Impact through the library volunteer page, or email volunteer@smcl.org.
notes: The page did not list a Teen Advisory Board. Roles are set by branch, and there may be a wait for an opening. Apply for your own branch (13 locations).
duration: 6 months or 1 semester

who_can_apply: California high school students who are at least 16 at the mid-June start. Preference goes to students living in San Diego or Imperial County. A few spots are reserved for San Diego MESA Alliance students.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Request Info' form on the SPARK page, or contact Program Director Sanjeev Ranade, PhD at cirmsparkinternship@sbpdiscovery.org.
notes: Confirm the current deadline before planning; the official page lists none. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 6 weeks, starting mid-June
pay_detail: Described as fully paid; the page does not state an amount.

who_can_apply: People currently enrolled in high school who can get a work permit. The page does not give a minimum age or a city residency rule.
how_to_apply: Check the city job site for internship openings and apply there. If none are open, check back later.
notes: Pay and hours are not stated. The job list loads by script, so open internships could not be checked on Oct 9, 2026. Other levels on the page are for college students.
duration: Not stated. Interns keep their spot by sending proof of school enrollment and their GPA after each semester.
pay_detail: Not stated. The city intern program page, checked on 2026-10-10, says nothing about pay. Check the job post when one is open.

who_can_apply: Volunteers age 12 and older. Under-18 volunteers use the minor waiver form in the Volunteer Handbook. Volunteers 18 and older get an online background check after a first review. Zoo volunteer jobs need a TB test.
how_to_apply: Fill out the forms in the Volunteer Handbook. Then send a volunteer form on the city volunteer page with the forms attached. Roles with children need extra forms.
notes: Ages 18 and up also do an online background check. Open roles were not listed on the page.
duration: Varies by role
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Santa Ana residents ages 16 to 24 who are U.S. citizens or have legal permission to work in the U.S. Youth under 18 must submit a Request for Work Permit.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application and upload the required documents. Youth under 18 must submit a Request for Work Permit form. Selection is first come, first served and spaces are limited. Call (714) 565-2600 or email SAYEmployment@santa-ana.org to confirm.
notes: Two city pages describe the same program with slightly different rules. Call (714) 565-2600 or email SAYEmployment@santa-ana.org to confirm which one fits you. The interest form is for a reopening notice. The main page says applications are open. The interest page says the program is closed to new applications.
duration: 15 to 20 hours a week; hours are flexible around school
pay_detail: Paid. The pay rate is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 12 years old with an adult, or 15 years old on their own. Zoo Buddies is for ages 12 to 14, who must volunteer with a parent or guardian age 18 or older, and both complete the requirements together.
how_to_apply: Long-term volunteers and Zoo Buddies apply with the online volunteer application on the zoo page. Short-term volunteers contact the zoo through its Contact Us page. The zoo does not accept walk-up volunteers.
notes: Short-term needs the City of Santa Ana one-time volunteer waiver. Long-term needs the city volunteer application, a TB test and a background check. The City of Santa Ana volunteer page says volunteers under 18 must complete a minor waiver form. The Santa Ana library teen volunteer program was not listed because the only page found was from 2021.
duration: Short-term: 40 hours or less (Greeter shifts Fri to Sun, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.). Long-term: more than 40 hours (shifts every day, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Cadets ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: Contact the squadron to set up a visit (the page says to let them know you are interested so they can schedule one). Meetings are at 629 Firestone Rd # B, Goleta, CA 93117. Phone: 805-822-4817. Email: Tyler.Epley@cawgcap.org (Deputy Commander for Cadets).
notes: Confirm first: the squadron pages do not list dues. The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.
duration: The squadron meets every Wednesday from 6:00 to 8:30 p.m. and has one Saturday activity a month.
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron pages do not list its own dues.

who_can_apply: Volunteers 16 and older. Volunteers 15 or younger are welcome with an adult partner. This is a parent or guardian volunteer who goes to training and works next to them.
how_to_apply: Dog roles are full at the Santa Barbara campus; the page also says its animal positions are full at this time, so confirm before applying. Clinic and outreach applications are listed. Fill out the online application for the role you want (dog, cat or clinic) and pick an orientation date and time. Outreach applications go by email. Main phone: 805-964-4777, or use the contact form on the page.
notes: Confirm first: the dog and cat roles were full when checked, and the page gives two different time commitments. Younger volunteers need a parent or guardian to volunteer with them.
duration: The page asks for at least 8 to 12 hours a month, and in another place at least two hours a week for 4 to 6 months.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18 interested in art or working with children. The program is competitive.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here links on the museum page for each class or camp. Email communityprograms@sbma.net or call 805-884-6457.
notes: The museum also runs a free SBPL x SBMA Teen Art Party for grades 7-12 (next: Jan 22, 2027 and Apr 16, 2027, Fridays 4-5:30 PM).
duration: Per class or camp: Winter After-School Class Tuesdays Jan 12 to Feb 16, 2027 (3:30-5:15 PM); Spring Camp Mar 29 to Apr 2, 2027 (9 AM-3 PM)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Counts toward required community service hours.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. Uniform shirt required: $20 (waived for teens with SNAP/Cal Fresh EBT).
how_to_apply: Fill in the online CIT application form. Contact Haylee Rosso at hrosso@sbnature2.org or 805-682-4711 ext. 170.
notes: Dates shown are the 2026 cycle. The page says summer CITs are invited back for fall, winter and spring break camps.
duration: At least 3 full weeks of camp (2026 camps ran June 15 to Aug 14)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours. $20 uniform shirt (waived with SNAP/CalFresh EBT).

who_can_apply: Students currently in 8th or 9th grade with at least a 2.5 GPA who can give 20 hours a month in the school year and 25 hours a week in summer, and have reliable transportation to the Museum and Sea Center.
how_to_apply: Online application, then an in-person interview. Contact Teen Programs Manager Haylee Rosso at hrosso@sbnature2.org or 805-682-4711 ext. 170.
notes: Only 8th and 9th graders can apply, so start early. Summers are intensive. Dates shown are the 2026 cycle; expect a similar early-spring deadline next year and check the page.
duration: 3 to 4 years; stay active year-round until graduation
pay_detail: Unpaid for the first 60 community service hours, then paid Museum employee shifts. The pay rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17 who can work a two-hour shift on Saturdays or Sundays during Museum hours (10 AM to 5 PM). Teens must buy a Museum Store shirt as a uniform; the cost is waived for teens with SNAP/CalFresh EBT.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online VolunTEEN application. Contact Haylee Rosso at hrosso@sbnature2.org or 805-682-4711 ext. 170.
notes: Dates shown are the 2026 cycle. Expect applications to reopen around April 1, 2027 (the page did not say).
duration: Up to 16 two-hour weekend shifts, Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day (2026: May 23 to Sept 6)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours for the SBUSD graduation requirement. Uniform shirt purchase required (waived with SNAP/CalFresh EBT).

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Use the Register button on the Teens and Early Adults page.
notes: The same page also lists a Job Apprentice Program and a free Arts Alliance mentoring program; those pages gave no ages or pay, so they are not listed.
duration: Summer camp season; length not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteer service hours.

who_can_apply: Eligibility varies by position. Some need experience or certifications (for example lifeguard); others are for first-time workers. Camp Recreation Assistants need no experience. Minimum ages are set in each job posting and were not read.
how_to_apply: Apply to open positions on the City's NEOGOV job site (Parks and Recreation). Lifeguard jobs include a tryout.
notes: The City has offered a reduced-cost lifeguard certification course for ages 15 and up (March 2024 notice, $50 for residents); check sbparksandrec.santabarbaraca.gov for the current course. Under-18 workers need a work permit from their school district. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Summer camps and pools; aquatics hires through the year with more hiring before summer
pay_detail: Hourly, set by position. A March 2024 City notice listed $18.78 to $23.92 an hour for lifeguards, camp counselors and swim instructors; no 2026 range is posted on the program page, so check the current posting.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 9 to 12. Parents and guardians are welcome. No registration needed for the fair; the interview workshop needs registration.
how_to_apply: Just show up. Sign up separately for the Teen Interview Skills Workshop.
notes: 2026 employers included the Museum of Natural History and Sea Center, MOXI, Santa Barbara Museum of Art, Santa Barbara Zoo, City Parks and Recreation, and the Postal Service. More than 200 teens attended in 2025.
duration: One afternoon, 2 hours
pay_detail: Free to attend. Employers offer summer jobs, internships and volunteer roles, but the page does not say if they are paid.

who_can_apply: Teens. Book reviews are for grades 7 to 12. The Teen Advisory Board is for high school students and requires a Library Services Orientation for Teens first. Volunteers ages 16 and over are welcome to complete an 8-hour training.
how_to_apply: Teen Volunteer Time: pre-register to guarantee a spot, or drop in. Advisory Board: send in the application and go to the orientation. Book reviews: send them through the library form.
notes: The apply link is the Teen Advisory Board form. Service-hour sign-off requests go to the Teen Services Librarian and take up to 3 business days. The library cannot sign court-ordered community service.
duration: Teen Volunteer Time: Thursdays 4:15 PM at Central Library (or Saturdays 11 AM to 12:30 PM at Eastside Library). Advisory Board: twice a month on Tuesdays, 5-6:30 PM, during the school year and once a month during the summer.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours (1 hour per book review, up to 5 reviews a month).

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 with strong communication skills, an interest in coding or robotics, and the ability to work well with teens and children. No experience needed. Limited spots for highly motivated teens.
how_to_apply: Online application form (linked from the library news post).
notes: Meets at Central Library, 40 E. Anapamu St. Posted October 4, 2026, so the deadline is close. Supported by a federal library grant.
duration: November 2026 to June 2027, about 2 hours a week (schedule to be set)
pay_detail: Unpaid. About 52 community service hours in total.

who_can_apply: High school and home school students. High-school-based courses are for Santa Barbara and Carpinteria Unified students only. Some courses are restricted. Complete the SBCC application and the dual enrollment steps first.
how_to_apply: Apply to SBCC through CCCApply, then follow the Steps to Enrollment for your course type. Contact dualenrollment@sbcc.edu or 805-898-8170.
notes: Your school counselor or College and Career Center can help choose courses.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: Applying to SBCC is free. High-school-based courses cost nothing. For online and campus courses, enrollment fees are waived but students pay student fees and textbooks.

who_can_apply: Anyone age 11 and up. Volunteers 11 to 13 must volunteer with a parent or guardian. Aquarist volunteers must be 14 or older. The Museum's adult page says some volunteers go on to advanced training after 48 hours of service. Commit to one shift a week for at least four months.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online volunteer application, interview, then attend mandatory training. Contact scvolunteer@sbnature2.org or 805-962-2526 ext. 110.
notes: Counts for the community service hours needed to graduate from high school in Santa Barbara Unified (per the Museum). Shifts are 9:45-12:45, 12:30-3:30 or 3:00-5:00.
duration: One shift per week for at least 4 months
pay_detail: Unpaid. A $45 program fee covers uniform, badge and administration; email scvolunteer@sbnature2.org for a fee waiver before your first training.

who_can_apply: High school students in 10th or 11th grade with a weighted GPA of at least 3.80. Students must attend the whole program and cannot take other courses or programs at the same time. No English test is needed for international applicants.
how_to_apply: Online application with a transcript that includes fall 2026 grades, AP scores if any, a 500-word personal statement, short answers, and the $75 fee. Tick the box on the application if you want to be considered for a scholarship. An optional info webinar is offered.
notes: Competitive. Costs shown are the 2026 figures because the 2027 cost page was not updated. Residential students live on campus and housing is billed by Summer Discovery. Contact: precollege@summer.ucsb.edu.
duration: About 7 weeks (June 14 to July 30, 2027 per the overview page; the admissions page says July 31).
pay_detail: 2026 cost page (the 2027 price is not posted): commuter $5,675 total ($75 application fee + $1,000 deposit + $5,600 tuition and program fees); residential $13,274 total (adds $7,599 housing and meals). A limited number of need-based scholarships exist, with priority for California residents.

who_can_apply: High school students in 9th, 10th or 11th grade with a weighted GPA of at least 3.60. Students must attend the whole program and cannot take other courses or programs at the same time. No English test is needed for international applicants.
how_to_apply: Online application with a transcript that includes fall 2026 grades, a 500-word personal statement, short answers, and the $75 fee. Tick the box on the application if you want to be considered for a scholarship. An optional info webinar is offered.
notes: Costs shown are the 2026 figures because the 2027 cost page was not updated. The younger, shorter and cheaper of the two UCSB pre-college programs. Contact: precollege@summer.ucsb.edu.
duration: About 4 weeks (June 25 to July 23, 2027 per the overview page; the admissions page says July 24).
pay_detail: 2026 cost page (the 2027 price is not posted): commuter $3,475 total ($75 application fee + $900 deposit + $3,400 tuition and program fees); residential $9,874 total (adds $6,399 housing and meals). A limited number of need-based scholarships exist, with priority for California residents.

who_can_apply: Volunteers are 18 or older. Teens ages 13 to 17 may volunteer alongside a guardian (an adult over 25 approved by the guardian is also allowed, per the FAQ). Email for the minor rules.
how_to_apply: Use Apply to Volunteer on the page (online form). For minors, email volunteer@sbwcn.org or call (805) 681-1080.
notes: Teens cannot volunteer alone. The page lists no youth-only program. Confirm first with the volunteer team how it works for a teen and guardian.
duration: Weekly 4-hour shift for most roles (not rescue and transport roles)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 19. Of 15 members, 8 must live in the City; seats are set aside for SBUSD high schools, alternative and private high schools, and at-large. Members serve two-year terms from July 1.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the City's advisory group application. Youth Council applicants interview with both the City Council and the current Youth Council. Contact Recreation Specialist Nicole Morgan, 805-897-2582.
notes: The City's recruitment page lists Youth Council interview dates but this check did not confirm which seats are open this round, so call Nicole Morgan. The City also has a one-year Youth Intern seat on some boards and commissions (nominated by a high school principal).
duration: Two-year term, July 1 to June 30. Meets the 1st and 3rd Monday at 5:15 PM at Franklin Neighborhood Center (monthly in July and August).
pay_detail: Unpaid (the City lists compensation as none).

who_can_apply: Most of our job opportunities are open to applicants 14 years and older; some positions require that an applicant be at least 16 or 18. You must be able to present proof of citizenship or legal right to work in the United States. Most positions require some related experience and/or an educational background in a related field. Students with no prior work experience: 'We will consider your application for our entry level positions.'
how_to_apply: Apply online for a specific opening on the Zoo's Employment Listings page. Send one application per job.
notes: The Careers page links to the Employment Listings on sbzoo.careerplug.com. It posted no specific openings when read, so check whether any are open now. Under-18 workers need a work permit from their school district. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Seasonal, mostly spring and summer
pay_detail: Not stated on the page; see each job listing.

who_can_apply: Current junior high or high school students. Junior Camp Counselors give at least 3 weeks of summer Zoo Camp (about 100 hours). Leaders in Training give 4 summer weeks (about 130 hours). Special-event volunteers can be 13 or older.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply links under Teens on the Zoo volunteer page. They are for the junior camp counselor application plus a reference letter. Call or email the Zoo to confirm before you plan.
notes: Confirm first. The Zoo says no internships are available at this time. The Zoo held a Job and Volunteer Fair on February 22 (year not on the page).
duration: Junior Camp Counselor: 7 hours a day, Mon-Fri, 3 summer weeks plus 1 fall week and 2 winter weeks
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18 who live in Santa Clara County.
how_to_apply: Join the waitlist form on the Teen CERT website or email scctcert@gmail.com to be told when the next academy opens. Paperwork drop-off happened before the last academy.
notes: The March 2026 flyer said ages 13 to 17 and the website says 13 to 18, so check your age with them. Cost is not stated; the last academy was at Los Altos Hills Town Hall. Santa Clara County residents only.
duration: 3 day academy (Friday evening to Sunday)
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Santa Clara residents ages 12 to 19. You cannot be employed by the City of Santa Clara.
how_to_apply: Apply during the yearly recruitment. Call the Youth and Teen Center at 408-615-3760 or email youthcommission@santaclaraca.gov to ask when it opens.
notes: Meets the second Tuesday of the month at 6 p.m. at the Youth and Teen Center, 2446 Cabrillo Ave. The page was last updated 2026-09-30.
duration: September to May, up to six years

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 7 to 12. No age range is stated. New members are always welcome.
how_to_apply: Use the Volunteer/TAB Sign Up link. It is at santaclaritavolunteers.com. Or contact a volunteer coordinator. They work at the Old Town Newhall library. They also work at the Canyon Country Jo Ann Darcy library and the Valencia library.
notes: Meeting dates are on the TAB Schedule calendar linked from the page. Branch coordinator emails are on the page.
duration: Meetings September through May
pay_detail: Unpaid. Participation can earn service hours (the number is not stated).

who_can_apply: High school students from schools across Santa Barbara County. Past members came from Lompoc, Orcutt, Santa Barbara, Santa Maria, Santa Ynez Valley and Carpinteria high schools.
how_to_apply: Use the Google form linked on the Student Advisory Council page.
notes: Confirm first: no ages, selection steps or deadline on the page. Past and current members are listed by district and school.
duration: One-year term that matches the school year
pay_detail: No pay stated.

who_can_apply: Students ages 15 to 18 who go to a public high school in Santa Barbara County.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now student form on the page or book a call through the Calendly link there. Phone: (805) 964-4711.
notes: Internship needs a current work permit, a photo ID and a Social Security card. You can take the training without those but get no stipend. This year 10 internship spots are for students interested in energy. Office: 3970 La Colina Rd, Suite 9.
duration: Training is about 1 hour a week for 7 or 8 weeks (page says both). Internship is at least 10 hours a week, 80 hours total.
pay_detail: Internships pay minimum wage. A stipend is possible for the training (amount not stated; needs a W-9 and a Social Security card or TIN).

who_can_apply: Local high school students. 10 high school and 10 college students are chosen, in screenwriter and director pairs. No age or grade rule or county rule is stated.
how_to_apply: The page gives no steps. A pair can submit one script and one film sample. Questions: claire@sbiff.org.
notes: Competitive: only 20 local students are chosen. Past high school participants came from Santa Barbara High, San Marcos and Dos Pueblos. Composers (college students) are also added.
duration: About 5 months, ending with the festival (Feb 3 to 13, 2027)
pay_detail: Free to students. No pay. Winning student directors get a prize camera package.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 18 who get CalWORKs benefits, or current and former foster youth ages 16 to 24. Open to year-round employment services.
how_to_apply: Call 408-758-3797 to begin your application, or use the Register/Refer form on the page.
notes: Only for teens who get CalWORKs benefits or who are/were in foster care, so most teens do not qualify. Under 18 needs a work permit. Positions are across the county.
duration: 8 weeks per cohort
pay_detail: $19.75 per hour, up to 30 hours per week

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 14 or older.
how_to_apply: Apply through the volunteer page at sccld.org/volunteer. Or ask a local library.
notes: Serves the library district branches, not every city in the county (San Jose has its own library). Hours, training and schedule are on the volunteer page. See the separate homework-help tutor card (Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteer Tutor) for a similar after-school tutoring role.

who_can_apply: High school student (regular, alternative vocational, or working toward equivalency), enrolled or graduated within 6 months, legal right to work in the US, overall GPA of at least 2.5. Application plus transcript and proof of enrollment. Under 18 needs a work permit (from your counselor or EDD). May need Live Scan and a physical.
how_to_apply: Subscribe to alerts for the Student Intern Level I posting on the county jobs site and apply with your transcript when it opens. You can also email departments, or the coordinator at studentinterns@esa.sccgov.org.
notes: Interns can be hired any time of year depending on department needs, so keep the alert on. Some departments (District Attorney, Behavioral Health, Public Health, Parks) run their own internships; contact them directly.
pay_detail: Paid on a five-step county salary scale; the rate is not stated on the page (see the county salary plan).

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. You must be free one afternoon, Monday to Thursday, from 3:30 to 6pm for a whole semester. You also need about 7 hours of training.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Application PDF from the library's volunteer page. Then upload it using the online form on that page.
notes: The page lists these libraries: Campbell, Cupertino, Gilroy, Los Altos, Milpitas, Morgan Hill and Saratoga. Check that your branch is on the list. Training is online (about 7 hours). The broader card (Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteers) also includes after-school tutoring of a kindergarten to grade 6 student.
duration: One semester

who_can_apply: Not stated on the page. Which classes you can take depends on your school district. Ask your counselor.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Ask your school counselor and look at the SCOE CTE course catalog. Contacts listed: Michelle McIntosh (Director), mmcintosh@scoe.net; Raelynn Sharp (Project Specialist), rsharp@scoe.net.
notes: The pages describe CTE (career technical education, 15 industry sectors) and list staff contacts. They do not list eligibility, enrollment steps, dates or work-based learning details. Treat this as a starting point and call SCOE. Age and grade are not stated, so ask your counselor.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 15 years old. Teens apply through the same process as adults; there is no separate teen program on the page.
how_to_apply: Submit one online application and choose one site. If chosen, you complete an interview, show proof of required immunizations and attend orientation. Onboarding takes about 6 to 8 weeks.
notes: Drop-in or on-call volunteering is not available. You pick a regular weekly shift. South region sites (Mercy San Diego, Chula Vista) take applications all the time. North region sites (Memorial La Jolla, Encinitas, Green) take them twice a year. Those times start on the first business day of April and October. Other applications are not reviewed. Only send one application.
duration: At least 6 months and 100 service hours; 2 to 4 hours a week depending on age and position
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Age 15 or older. You must give one 4-hour shift a week for at least six months in a row and at least 100 hours. They cannot take summer-only or school-break-only volunteers.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application and a volunteer reference form, then interview, attend a 2-hour orientation, pass a background check and health screening.
notes: The health screening asks for proof of vaccines, a flu shot, immunity to measles, mumps, rubella and varicella, a Tdap shot, and a TB test within the last 3 months. Ask your parent to start gathering records early. Questions: vmcvolunteer@hhs.sccgov.org.
duration: At least 6 months and 100 hours

who_can_apply: High school students. The page gives no narrower age or grade range. Space is limited to 12 teens.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application on the Teens page. Only completed forms are considered. Questions: outreach@sdmart.org.
notes: Closed right now. Check the page around late summer 2027 for the next application.
duration: October 2026 to end of June 2027; monthly meetings on Zoom with several in-person events
pay_detail: No stipend or fee stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students ages 6 to 18. Many students join through partner schools; some workshops allow direct sign-up.
how_to_apply: Check the calendar on the 826 Valencia site or contact a Writing Center.
notes: All 826 Valencia programs are free, and most students join through partner schools. The stipended Youth Leadership Advisory Board (grades 8 to 12) and Black Literary Achievement Club are listed on the SFPL page; the stipend amount is not posted.
duration: Varies
pay_detail: Free programs; some leadership roles are stipended (amounts not posted)

who_can_apply: Any current high school student in grades 9 to 12. Preference goes to students in Breakthrough now. It also goes to people who are or were Breakthrough volunteers.
how_to_apply: Fill in the notify form on the BLP page to hear when the summer 2027 application opens.
notes: Breakthrough's separate Teaching Fellow job is a paid summer teaching residency with housing for people from outside SF and does not say it is for high schoolers, so it is not listed here. Located at 350 Masonic Ave.
duration: Summer 2026 ran orientation June 15 to 18, then June 22 to July 31, 2026, about 6 weeks
pay_detail: Rate not posted. Paid through San Francisco's Opportunities for All program. Some hours also count toward school volunteer requirements.

who_can_apply: Current 9th or 10th graders at an SFUSD school, with a 2.5 GPA and a C or higher in science and math, authorized to work in the US, able to commit 2 to 3 years through high school, and able to get to the Academy after school and on Saturdays.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window opens in February 2027. Contact CiS@calacademy.org.
notes: SFUSD students only. Sign up for the Academy's Youth Programs mailing list to hear when applications open. Questions: CiS@calacademy.org.
duration: 2 to 3 years through graduation
pay_detail: Paid above minimum wage (rate not posted)

who_can_apply: SFUSD high school students, through a partnership with City College. Talk to your high school counselor about which classes are offered. Non-SFUSD students, or SFUSD students who want a class their school does not offer, use the Concurrent Enrollment page.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor. Questions: dualenrollment@ccsf.edu. Non-SFUSD students use the CCSF Concurrent Enrollment page.
notes: Classes can be at your high school or at a CCSF location. A permission consent form for high school students is linked on the page. Grade and credit rules are not stated on the page, so ask your counselor.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24. Register with the Google Form on the DCYF listing.
how_to_apply: Register using the form linked from the sf.gov youth opportunities page. Bring a resume if you have one.
notes: The page does not list which employers will attend. It is a free event, not a job offer.
duration: Wed Oct 14, 2026, 12 to 4 p.m.
pay_detail: Free to attend. Employers share job openings, but the page does not say if those jobs are paid.

who_can_apply: San Francisco high school students. No prior experience needed.
how_to_apply: Watch the Department of Elections high school programs page for the next application. Questions: hsp@sfgov.org or 415-558-6100.
notes: Same page: if you will be 16 by the next Election Day you can apply to be a high school poll worker, with a stipend up to $245. A poll worker application for the November 2026 election was due to be posted there in mid-August.
duration: About 2 weeks: Sept 14 to 27 in fall 2026, plus a 90 minute in-person training
pay_detail: Unpaid. Ambassadors get a participation certificate signed by the Mayor and community service hours.

who_can_apply: High school age students, 15 to 18 for first-time Explainers (up to 20 for returning ones). Must be able to get a work permit, attend all training dates and work the whole school year or summer session. No science background needed.
how_to_apply: When open, apply on the Exploratorium Current Openings page under the job title High School Explainer. Questions: hsesupervisors@exploratorium.edu.
notes: About 130 paid positions a year across two cohorts. The Current Openings list did not show on my read, so check it for a live posting. A separate PACE program serves ages 17 to 21.
duration: A summer session or a school-year session, with over 60 hours of training (20 before working with visitors)
pay_detail: Paid job; the wage is not on the program page

who_can_apply: Cadets must attend high school in San Francisco (or equivalent) or live in the City and County of San Francisco. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page on the academy's website.
notes: The site does not list an age range or application dates, so ask the academy. It is a project of the SF Black Firefighters Association. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Saturdays 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., following the SFUSD calendar. A 2025 news article said 15 weeks each fall.
pay_detail: Free to join. Cadets get breakfast, lunch and a bi-weekly stipend (amount not stated).

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18 and in high school. The page says teens on Heart&Sole teams must identify as female, and males are welcome on Girls on the Run teams. Needs a completed reference, a signed waiver (parent signs if under 18) and the Junior Coach application. Background check at 18.
how_to_apply: Complete the Junior Coach application on the Girls on the Run Bay Area site. Email admin@gotrbayarea.org or call (415) 863-8942 to ask about late spots or the next season.
notes: The Oct 12, 2026 date on the sf.gov listing is for adult coaches (18 and up), not Junior Coaches. Teams meet at least once a week.
duration: 8 to 10 weeks, 1.5 to 3 hours per week; season starts early September, 5K on Nov 14, 2026
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 (high school). Priority goes to youth underrepresented in tech, students at high schools with few or no computer science classes, and girls and LGBTQIA+ youth. Online classes are for San Francisco students only.
how_to_apply: Pick a class. Then register on the Mission Bit Classes page when registration opens.
notes: Mission Bit's Tech Start career prep is ages 18 to 26, not for most high schoolers. College Connections (Nov 7, 2026, 10:30 a.m. to noon at Chase Center, grades 9 to 12) closes registration Oct 27, 2026 per sf.gov.
duration: Semester long. Fall 2026 classes ran Sep 8 to Dec 4, 2026.
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: San Francisco youth ages 14 to 17 (the DCYF newsletter lists grades 9 and 10 for this round). Apply through the JCYC Workhub.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the JCYC Workhub (jcycworkhub.org). Ask the YMCA contact on the page about your neighborhood site.
notes: Pay rate is not stated on the pages, so ask your site. Contact the Buchanan YMCA ((415) 931-9622) about eligibility.
duration: School year: Oct to April, with an 8 hour per week internship Jan to April. Summer: June to August, 20 hours per week.
pay_detail: Paid work experience (hourly rate not posted on the program pages)

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24. Aimed at 'opportunity youth' who are out of school or not working.
how_to_apply: Apply on the New Door intake portal linked from their site. The application link is on the official page.
notes: Mainly for 17 year olds and older who are not in a regular school path; not the usual fit for a student who is in school. Pay is not stated on the pages.
duration: 6 months
pay_detail: Paid (rate not posted)

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 24 who live and/or go to school in San Francisco, per the JCYC Workhub OFA page.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the JCYC Workhub, complete the application and submit before the spring deadline.
notes: JCYC runs the applications. B2SF and the OFA fellowships share an application with other youth programs. Your interests decide where you are placed.
duration: B2SF is 6 weeks; OFA length not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Paid; the hourly rate and hours are not posted on the program pages

who_can_apply: California residents ages 16 and 17 who are US citizens and not in prison for a felony or ruled mentally unable to vote by a court.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online form at registertovote.ca.gov (linked from the Secretary of State page).
notes: Not a job or internship, but a real civic step. Your registration becomes active when you turn 18. Citizenship is required.
duration: A few minutes
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: San Francisco high school students (there are separate college tracks). The application page says details are coming soon.
how_to_apply: Use the High School Internship application page. Questions: sfprojectpull1996@gmail.com.
notes: The pages do not list age, pay or a deadline yet. Check the application page in early 2027.
duration: About 8 weeks (per the SFPUC page)
pay_detail: Paid (rate not posted on the program page)

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 in San Francisco.
how_to_apply: Email yep@sfgov.org or call Yuri Ugarte at 415-452-3863. The page's email link shows rec-yep@sfgov.org, so confirm which address works.
notes: This page replaced the older Workreation name on the department site. An older listing says applicants need work-permit papers and no citizenship is required.
duration: Up to 25 hours per week in summer; 10 hours per week in the school year
pay_detail: Pay not posted on the program page

who_can_apply: No minimum age is listed for youth volunteers. If a branch is not on the application form, it cannot take volunteers right now.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online volunteer form at https://on.sfpl.org/yva
notes: FOG Readers tutoring takes some volunteers age 15 and up. It needs a 6 month commitment and fingerprinting. The same page lists paid teen jobs. YELL is a summer job, and applications open each March. The Youth Advisory Board closed applications for this year on Sept 14.
duration: Ongoing; some roles start late October or early November
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students from San Francisco's southeast neighborhoods; internships start after junior year.
how_to_apply: The SFPUC page does not list an application. It says SFUSD students are referred through SFUSD's Career and Technical Education office, so ask them or the SFPUC workforce team.
notes: Narrow neighborhood focus (southeast San Francisco). The same SFPUC page also lists YouthWorks and Project Pull.
duration: Summer
pay_detail: Paid (rate not posted)

who_can_apply: Nature Trail: ages 12 to 14. Junior Zoologists: ages 15 to 17. Leadership Fellows: entering grades 10 to 12 in fall 2026 (ages 15 to 17 per the zoo's volunteer page).

Health requirements after acceptance include MMR, varicella, Tdap, COVID, flu and TB testing. Contact scv.volunteers@sharp.com or 619-502-3606. duration: Per term

who_can_apply: 16 or older (by June 2 in the 2026 cycle), current junior or senior, 2.5 GPA or higher, attends an eligible school in the service area, no relatives who work for the internship host, own transportation.

who_can_apply: High school students, per the page. The page does not state age, grade range, residency or citizenship rules.

duration: Not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Rising sophomores, juniors and seniors who are at least 14 and can commute daily to the Palo Alto campus. You need a laptop.

The apply page says a decision takes about 10 business days after your application is complete.

who_can_apply: High school students at partner schools in Sacramento, Solano, Shasta and Siskiyou counties who are low income or whose parents did not attend college.

who_can_apply: California high school students in grades 8 to 12, per the COSMOS application site. A GPA of 3.5 or above is typical.

duration: 5 weeks (June 22 to July 24 in 2026)
pay_detail: Pay or stipend not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students at participating schools. Upward Bound: freshmen or sophomores at Moreno Valley, Perris, Rubidoux, Banning, Norte Vista, Ramona, Bloomington, Colton or Eisenhower High School. Talent Search: Arroyo Valley, Indian Springs, Pacific, San Bernardino or San Gorgonio High. Both need a 2.5 GPA, U.S. citizenship or permanent residency, low income and/or first generation, and interest in college.
how_to_apply: Upward Bound: fill out the interest form on the page to get an application. Talent Search: fill out the ETS application. Give it to your school's ETS contact or email ets@ucr.edu. You can also call the TRIO office at (951) 827-4865.
notes: Only students at the listed schools qualify. The page does not list grade levels for Talent Search.
duration: Year-round support; UB summer program is 6 weeks (5 weeks bused to campus, final week in residence halls)
pay_detail: Free to join. Only Upward Bound summer participants receive a stipend (amount not stated).

who_can_apply: Motivated students completing grades 8 through 12 with strong interest and achievement in math and science. In 2026 the in-person program was limited to California residents. Students can attend COSMOS only once.
how_to_apply: Online application through the COSMOS portal: choose UCSD, rank two clusters and write an essay for each, one or two online recommendations from a math or science teacher, current and prior-year transcripts, and the application fee.
notes: 2027 dates come from the statewide COSMOS site; the UCSD page still shows 2026 dates. Fees shown are for 2026. 2026 rules asked for proof of COVID vaccination and a negative test; check whether that still applies. If admitted, a non-refundable deposit of one third of tuition holds your spot.
duration: 4 weeks (2026: July 5 to July 31)
pay_detail: 2026 program cost $5,518 (housing, meals, field trips) plus a $46 application fee. Financial assistance form available for California residents. Amounts for 2027 not posted.

who_can_apply: Incoming 11th and 12th graders with a cumulative GPA of 3.3 or better who are interested in sports medicine. No application is needed; you enroll directly.
how_to_apply: Enroll directly on the Extended Studies registration page. Add the course to your cart. No application or essay is needed. Questions: precollege@ucsd.edu.
notes: Earns 3 to 6 UC pre-college units. UCSD's Research Scholars also offers life sciences and marine science courses; its older Academic Connections summer program was canceled for 2026. Marine science fall 2026 application closed Sept 17, 2026.
duration: 3 weeks, weekdays 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. (2026: July 6 to July 24)
pay_detail: $3,500 for the July 2026 session (commuter only; no housing or transportation). A hybrid fall session cost $2,000.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. You must be 18 to volunteer in pediatric inpatient units or the Emergency Department. Minimum 6 months, one 3 to 4 hour weekday shift each week.
how_to_apply: Attend a virtual info session, in-person group interview, online training and health clearance (background check if 18+). Volunteer Services (415) 502-9888.
notes: The Oct 13 opening is for Parnassus and Mt. Zion or Mission Bay programs in San Francisco, not Oakland. UCSF says it cannot take new volunteers for other roles right now. Under 18 needs a parent at the health clearance visit. No high school summer program was found on the official pages.
duration: One weekly 3 to 4 hour shift for 6 months

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 who live in or go to school in Union City.
how_to_apply: Submit an application between February 1 and April 1, then interview in April.
notes: Follow @UCTeens on Instagram for events, per the city page. The program runs out of the Kennedy Youth Center.
duration: August to May

who_can_apply: US citizen (the Senate application guide also mentions permanent residents; ask the office) with a Social Security number. Must be 16 or 17 at appointment, a junior (semester) or one who has completed the sophomore year (summer), with a 3.0 GPA and health forms. Needs a Senator's sponsorship. Senator Padilla sponsors California residents only.
how_to_apply: Send a cover letter, resume, recent high school transcript and two recommendation letters to Senator Padilla's office. The page lists Page_Program@padilla.senate.gov as the contact for questions and does not say where to submit, so confirm the submission address with the office. Other Senate offices have their own rules; the central Page Program does not take applications.
notes: Pages pay their own travel to and from Washington, DC. The job is in DC, so a California work permit likely does not apply; ask the office. Moving to DC for a semester is a big step for a family.
duration: Spring 2027 session: Jan 24 to June 4, 2027. Summer 2027 dates to be announced.
pay_detail: $35,360 per year, prorated

who_can_apply: High school juniors or seniors holding an elected or appointed leadership office this school year, such as student body or class officer. Must be a US citizen or green card holder and live in California. Get the application from your principal, counselor or social studies teacher, or the state contact.
how_to_apply: Ask your principal or counselor for the application, or email the California coordinator at ussyp@cde.ca.gov (California Department of Education, Sacramento).
notes: Very competitive. Clubs, debate, Model UN, jobs and self-made groups do not count as qualifying offices. The CDE page was blocked by a bot check, so the coordinator name and contact are from the USSYP site only. If you are a junior now, plan for next fall.
duration: Washington Week March 6 to 13, 2027
pay_detail: $12,500 college scholarship; travel, hotel and meals paid by the Hearst Foundations

who_can_apply: High school students who have completed ninth grade by the start of the program and are pursuing a rigorous curriculum. Domestic and international students may apply.
how_to_apply: Online application with the $85 fee. Email summer@usc.edu with questions.
notes: Expensive. The admissions page does not describe financial aid, so ask summer@usc.edu. The prices and dates above are the 2026 numbers and may change for 2027.
duration: Four weeks, 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. each class day (2026 classes began June 22)
pay_detail: 2026 total for domestic students: $8,130 commuter or $11,570 residential. That adds tuition $7,401, course materials $300, program fee $325 and health center $104; residential adds $3,440 room and board. Also a $85 nonrefundable application fee and a $1,000 deposit that counts toward the total.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 8 to 11 in 2026, rising grades 9 to 12. Active MESA, Mission Science and Engineering Transformer students come first. So do students at STEM Center schools. All students are considered.
how_to_apply: When it is open, send a student form and a teacher recommendation. You can use the online form or the PDF. Forms that are not complete are not considered. Contact k12summer@usc.edu.
notes: The page says in person at USC main campus. The USC Viterbi summer programs list calls it virtual. Confirm the format before you count on it.
pay_detail: Free to attend. No pay.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 and up for aircraft restoration, ship restoration, radio, community outreach and visitor services (16 and 17 year olds work with an adult). Collections: 18 and up. Docents, events, security: 21 and up.
how_to_apply: Apply at volgistics.com/appform/1737643431 or call (510) 521-8448 ext. 243.
notes: Ship work involves climbing ladders and tight spaces. Another museum page lists overnight programs for groups, but no teen intern program.
duration: Set weekly shifts, for example Wed and Sat 8:30 to noon (aircraft), Tue and Sat (ship), first Saturday monthly (radio)

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 (18-year-olds must be enrolled in high school). Based on the 2024 flyer; check the current year's rules.
how_to_apply: 2024 flyer: application with parent signature, a 1-page essay, an availability schedule, and a virtual orientation. Contact the VA Center for Development and Civic Engagement, vhalomyouthprogram@va.gov.
notes: Closed now. The age, hours and application steps come from the 2024 flyer because the current page only says 2026 applications are closed. The 2024 flyer also required COVID vaccination or an exemption; check the current policy.
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. (2024: June 17 to July 26)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Free to join; volunteers over 100 hours can be considered for scholarships through community partners (2024 flyer).

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18, attending high school in Santa Clara County and living in the county. Able to give up to 5 hours a month for 2 years, and attend quarterly Wednesday evening meetings in person.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Commission interest form. To apply you need to know your Valley Water board district (find your home address on the map on the page).
notes: Meetings are at Valley Water headquarters, 5700 Almaden Expressway, San Jose.
duration: 2-year term, up to 5 hours a month

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. Seniors are told not to apply because onboarding is long (a college program exists).
how_to_apply: Email volunteer_services@washingtonhealth.com with your name, grade, school, phone and email. They contact you only when an info session is scheduled. Phone 510-818-7465.
notes: No GPA rule or fee appears on the current page (older versions listed a GPA rule and $20 fee). Openings are limited. Office: 2500 Mowry Ave, Fremont. The page says the list is closed as of May 22, 2026, but also says you are welcome to join the list now; call to confirm.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 16, eligible West Sacramento residents. Needs proof of the hepatitis B vaccine series, fingerprinting and a background check.
how_to_apply: The page does not give application steps. Call the Club West Teen Center at (916) 373-5877 or ask City of West Sacramento Parks and Recreation.
notes: Page has no year or dates, so ask when applications open. Vaccine proof may take weeks to collect. Runs in summer.
pay_detail: Free to join, unpaid. The page does not list a stipend.

who_can_apply: Concurrent enrollment: grades 9 to 12. Middle College: juniors and seniors from LGSUHSD and CUHSD. Dual enrollment on high school campuses: CUHSD (Campbell Union High School District) students only.
how_to_apply: Start at the college's high school students page and apply through the admissions portal; the page also covers assessment, orientation and registration.
notes: Ask the college about unit limits and your counselor about credit.
pay_detail: Free (per the college page)

who_can_apply: Current high school students who have finished 8th grade. Partner high school classes are arranged through your counselor. Tuition is free for 11 units or fewer.
how_to_apply: Explore with your counselor, apply on CCCApply, set up your student account, submit the CCAP or High School Non-CCAP form, then register.
notes: Students may pay for books and materials. Check your counselor for term deadlines. Davis High was not on the CCAP list I saw, so a Davis student would use the non-CCAP route. Charter and homeschool students may need grade verification.
duration: Per term
pay_detail: Free up to 11 units ($46 per unit fee waived); books may cost

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Register online through the Woodland Community Services registration portal (linked from the Teen Programs page) or call (530) 661-2000. Email: WoodlandCSD@cityofwoodland.gov.
notes: The page gives no hours, dates or fees. Call Community Services to ask how it works and when to start.

who_can_apply: Santa Clara County residents ages 16 to 24 who are low-income and have at least one barrier to employment or education.
how_to_apply: Call the San Jose Job Center at 408-794-1101 or the Gilroy center at 408-758-3477 and ask about the young adult program.
notes: San Jose Works, a partner program, is also on the page. The page gives ages 14 to 18 for its Paid Work Experience Program and ages 16 to 29 for other city services. Income and barrier rules apply. The page does not say whether job centers are by appointment only. It does not say whether the other services are free.
pay_detail: Paid work experience; the page says you can earn up to $25 an hour.

who_can_apply: Washington Unified School District high school students who are 16 by the first day. River City HS students need a Career Technical Education course; Yolo HS and Washington Middle College students need a teacher or counselor recommendation. Everyone attends one online info session.
how_to_apply: Go to the Internships page, attend the info session, send the recommendation form if needed, then apply and interview with employers.
notes: Employers have included Center for Land Based Learning, Elica Health Centers, City of West Sacramento and others. The 2026 calendar on the page is an image, so ask for 2027 dates: wshomerun@cityofwestsacramento.org or (916) 617-4500.
duration: summer, up to 40 hours per week
pay_detail: Paid by the City of West Sacramento, up to 40 hours per week. Hourly rate not posted on the page.

who_can_apply: Students in Yolo County. Start through your school College and Career Center or counselor, or email CCR@ycoe.org. Age or grade limits were not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Tell your school College and Career Center or counselor, or email CCR@ycoe.org.
notes: B-Unbound is the online platform for finding opportunities (interviews, tours, job shadowing, projects, internships). Placement depends on available mentors, so ask early. The stipend is paid after you finish the requirements. Email: CCR@ycoe.org. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: About 60 hours
pay_detail: Stipend up to $500 on successful completion

who_can_apply: Oakland youth. YEP's job training serves ages 14 to 24. The City of Oakland's summer list shows YEP's summer program for ages 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: Use the application links on yep.org/how-you-join, or call 510-533-3447 or visit 2300 International Blvd, Oakland.
notes: The YEP page does not give pay rates. Age 14 to 18 for summer comes from the City of Oakland table; the 19 to 24 programs are for older youth.
duration: Summer: about 100 hours, June 1 to Sept 30 (City list). Afterschool jobs during the school year.
pay_detail: Paid; about 100 hours of work in the City summer program (hourly rate not posted)

who_can_apply: Ongoing volunteers must be at least 16. Teens 14 and older can volunteer at many special events. Volunteers under 18 need parental consent.
how_to_apply: The page has no general form. Open roles link to postings (examples: Tustin Expanded Learning Volunteer, Youth and Government MUN Volunteer, Sports Volunteer at Laguna Niguel). Questions go through the contact form at ymcaoc.org/contact-us/.
notes: All ongoing volunteers complete an online orientation, child abuse prevention training and role training. Screening includes an application, waiver, ID copy and background check, with extra checks for higher-responsibility roles. Court-ordered community service is not accepted. The YMCA of Orange County Model Legislature and Court page describes the statewide YMCA Youth and Government program, so it is not listed separately.
duration: Varies by role
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: The page lists the program for ages 14 to 24 and older. Grade level, residency and other rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. The page says to contact the Workforce Development team. Phone numbers listed: Urban Services YMCA (415) 561-0631; Bayview Hunters Point YMCA (415) 822-7728; Chinatown YMCA (415) 576-9622.
notes: This is an umbrella page for several branch programs. Season, wage, hours and deadlines are not stated, so call a branch before a teen applies. The ymcasf.org/teens page lists teens ages 13-18 across programs, but it gives no details for Workforce Development. Contact emails on the page are obfuscated and were not confirmed, so none are listed.
pay_detail: Paid internships are mentioned at the Urban Services YMCA. Wage and hours are not stated. Other activities are not described as paid.

who_can_apply: Must be at least 15 years old, in 10th grade or higher, and in good academic standing. A High School Authorization Form must be signed by members of your school. No prior training is required, according to the FAQ.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application on ymcasv.org (the Apply Today button on the cabin leaders page), get a High School Authorization Form signed by members of your school, and watch email for further instructions. The page recommends applying at least two weeks before your session dates.
notes: Camp Campbell is at 16275 Highway 9, Boulder Creek, CA 95006, per the cabin-leaders page. This is an unpaid volunteer role, so no work permit is needed. The same YMCA's Youth and Government program is already in ymca-youth-and-government-ca.json. Leaders in Training is also listed on the leadership page, but its age and details are not stated, so it is not a card.
duration: Five days per session (typically Monday to Friday). Session dates are not stated.
pay_detail: Pay not stated. The page says this is a way to earn Service-Learning credit for graduation.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12 from anywhere in California. Join a local delegation. Cost and sign-up steps are not posted on either page.
how_to_apply: Two ways to reach the program. Southern California: contact the program director at (626) 604-4210 or use the inquiry form on the YMCA of Orange County site. Silicon Valley area: click 'Sign up for more information' on the YMCA of Silicon Valley Leadership Development page, which opens the YMCA sign-up form. Neither page describes the application steps.
notes: Over 1,300 teens in more than 60 California delegations. The YMCA of Orange County page (Southern California) lists no Northern California contact. The YMCA of Silicon Valley lists the same statewide program and links a sign-up form for the Silicon Valley area. Ask the director which delegation serves your area, and ask about cost and scholarships. The YMCA of Silicon Valley Leadership Development page also lists other teen groups and a Model UN program for middle school students; they are not part of this entry.
duration: Weekly meetings plus conferences in November and February
pay_detail: The fee is not posted on either program page; ask your local YMCA about cost and scholarships

who_can_apply: Youth in Yolo County. The page does not list ages. Fee waivers are available.
how_to_apply: Find a community club, attend a meeting, complete online enrollment and pay the fee. Office: bbrinkhoushatch@ucanr.edu, 530-666-8703.
notes: Teens can take leader and ambassador roles. The fee is non-refundable. A fee waiver or reduction form is available. Returning members update their online enrollment and send health forms to their club.
pay_detail: 2026-27 enrollment is $80 per youth (waiver or reduction available).

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24, living in Yolo County, and not in school right now, per the page. The page names foster care, homelessness, disabilities, parenting, leaving high school, and justice involvement as challenges the program serves.
how_to_apply: Contact the Workforce Development Program Manager at the Administrative Offices, (530) 757-5558, or drop by free office hours on Wednesdays from 3 to 6 p.m. at 2455 West Capitol Ave, #118, West Sacramento, CA 95691.
notes: Only the 17-year-old end of this guide's 13 to 18 range is covered. Older YCCA posts mention up to 300 paid hours; that figure is not on the current page and is not used here. Narrower and competitive: it is aimed at young people facing barriers and out of school. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The pay rate and number of hours are not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Opportunities are limited and differ by branch. The Mary L. Stephens Davis Branch is not accepting applications right now. The page does not list a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Download the Youth Volunteer Application (PDF) from the volunteer page and email it or drop it off at the branch you want.
notes: Call the branch first (main number 530-666-8005). The page said the Mary L. Stephens Davis Branch was not accepting volunteer applications when checked.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 15 cannot volunteer alone. They must be with an adult or a supervised group. Ages 16 to 17 can volunteer alone with parent permission (youth waiver).
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Yolo Food Bank volunteer site. Use the Youth Volunteer Waiver for ages 12 to 17. Then sign up online for events. Email volunteer@yolofoodbank.org.
notes: Wear closed-toe shoes and gloves at events. You log your own hours in your volunteer account. Ages 12 to 15 must be with an adult or a supervised group.

who_can_apply: For the Service Award: students in grades K to 12 who live or go to school in Santa Clara or San Mateo County. High schoolers need 100 hours within 12 months. Other programs list no clear age rule.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Do Service platform at volunteer.youthcommunityservice.org. Phone 650-858-8019 or email ycs@youthcommunityservice.org.
notes: They also offer a scholarship and one-day service pop-ups. It is based at 780 Arastradero Rd, Palo Alto.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form linked on youthradio.org.
notes: The page describes training and mentoring, not a formal paid internship. Ask whether it is paid. It is not on the City of Oakland's 2026 summer jobs list.
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the site

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 25, low-income or homeless youth (per the Berkeley Public Library jobs page).
how_to_apply: Call (510) 858-7229 or email community@youthspiritartworks.org (both on the home page) and ask about job training. The Berkeley Public Library jobs page lists jobtraining@youthspiritartworks.org.
notes: Read the home page on 2026-10-09. It says YSA serves transitional age youth 14 to 25 at 1740 Alcatraz Ave, Berkeley, with free drop-in hours, workshops and events; some workshop series pay a $300 stipend for full participation. The home page does not describe a job training program or its pay, so the 15 to 25 age range, the paid jobs and the jobtraining email come from the library page and are unconfirmed. The FAQ says YSA is not actively accepting applications. Ask before you plan around a job. Not on the City of Oakland's 2026 summer jobs list.
pay_detail: Job training rate not posted (checked 2026-10-09). The home page lists a $300 stipend for full participation in some workshop series.

who_can_apply: East Oakland youth. The City of Oakland list shows YU summer jobs for ages 14 to 21. YU serves ages 13 to 24 overall.
how_to_apply: Call 510-777-9909 or visit 8711 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. The site gives no online form.
notes: YU's own site has no summer job details, so the ages and hours come from the City of Oakland's 2026 list. Also a referral partner for EBMUD's high school internship.
duration: About 100 hours over 4 to 6 weeks (City list)
pay_detail: Paid (100 hours of fully paid work per the City list); rate not posted

who_can_apply: Oakland middle and high school students. The City summer jobs list shows Media Careers for ages 16 to 21 (June to September).
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page at youthbeat.org/apply, or call 510-922-0060 or email youthbeatmedia@gmail.com.
notes: YouthBeat's own page does not state exact ages; 16 to 21 comes from the City of Oakland's list. Address is a PO box in Oakland.
pay_detail: Training is free; apprentice and PRO work is paid (rate not posted)
